sentences.zh: 楊洪，字宗道，六合人。

translations.literal: Yang Hong, style name Zongdao, was a native of Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hong, styled Zongdao, was from Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 祖政，明初以功為漢中百戶。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zheng, in the early Ming for merit became a company officer at Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zheng, rewarded in the early Ming for military service, became a company officer at Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 父璟，戰死靈璧。

translations.literal: His father Jing died in battle at Lingbi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing was killed in battle at Lingbi.

sentences.zh: 洪嗣職，調開平。

translations.literal: Hong succeeded to the post and was transferred to Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: Hong inherited the post and was posted to Kaiping.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，遇敵輒身先突陣。

translations.literal: He was skilled at mounted archery; whenever he met the enemy he would personally lead the charge into the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in horsemanship and archery, he always led the charge himself whenever he met the enemy.

sentences.zh: 初，從成祖北征，至斡難河，獲人馬而還。

translations.literal: At first, following the Yongle Emperor on the northern campaign, he reached the Onon River, captured men and horses, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he followed the Yongle Emperor on the northern campaign as far as the Onon River, took captives and horses, and returned.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「將才也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is the stuff of a general.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Here is a born commander.

sentences.zh: 」令識其名，進千戶。

translations.literal: " He ordered that his name be noted and promoted him to chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: " He had his name recorded and promoted him to chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年命以精騎二百，專巡僥塞上。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuande he was ordered to take two hundred picked horsemen and patrol exclusively along the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 4 he was ordered to take two hundred picked cavalry and patrol the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 繼命城西貓兒峪，留兵戍之。

translations.literal: He was next ordered to the Maor Valley west of the city and left troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: He was next posted to Maor Valley west of the city and left troops to garrison the place.

sentences.zh: 敗寇於紅山。

translations.literal: He defeated the raiders at Hongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the raiders at Hongshan.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，尚書王驥言邊軍怯弱，由訓練無人，因言洪能。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, Minister Wang Ji said the frontier troops were timid and weak because no one trained them, and on that account spoke of Hong's ability.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong came to the throne, Minister Wang Ji said the frontier armies had grown timid for lack of proper training and recommended Hong for the task.

sentences.zh: 詔加洪遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: An edict added to Hong the title of Mobile General.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Hong a Mobile General.

sentences.zh: 洪所部才五百，詔選開平、獨石騎兵益之，再進都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Hong's command numbered only five hundred; an edict selected cavalry from Kaiping and Dushi to augment them, and he was again promoted to Assistant Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's command numbered only five hundred men, so the court selected cavalry from Kaiping and Dushi to reinforce him and promoted him again to Assistant Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時先朝宿將已盡，洪後起，以敢戰著名。

translations.literal: At that time the veteran generals of the previous reign were all gone; Hong rose later and became famous for daring in battle.
translations.idiomatic: By then the veteran generals of the previous reign were gone, and Hong, who had risen later, was famed for his boldness in battle.

sentences.zh: 為人機變敏捷，善出奇搗虛，未嘗小挫。

translations.literal: As a man he was resourceful and quick, skilled at unexpected strikes against weak points, and never suffered a minor setback.
translations.idiomatic: Resourceful and quick-witted, he excelled at surprise attacks on weak points and never suffered even a minor defeat.

sentences.zh: 雖為偏校，中朝大臣皆知其能，有毀之者，輒為曲護，洪以是得展其才。

translations.literal: Although only a subordinate officer, ministers at court all knew his ability; when anyone slandered him they would bend the rules to protect him, and Hong thereby was able to display his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Though only a subordinate officer, court ministers all knew his worth; whenever anyone spoke against him they shielded him, and so Hong was able to put his talents fully to use.

sentences.zh: 尚書魏源督邊事，指揮杜衡、部卒李全皆訐奏洪罪。

translations.literal: Minister Wei Yuan supervised frontier affairs; Commander Du Heng and a soldier Li Quan all denounced Hong in memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wei Yuan was in charge of frontier affairs when Commander Du Heng and a soldier named Li Quan both denounced Hong in memorials.

sentences.zh: 帝從源言，謫衡廣西，執全付洪自治。

translations.literal: The emperor followed Yuan's words, banished Heng to Guangxi, and handed Quan over to Hong to punish as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Yuan's account, banished Heng to Guangxi, and handed Quan over to Hong to deal with as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 尋命洪副都督僉事李謙守赤城、獨石。

translations.literal: Soon Hong was ordered to assist Vice Commander Li Qian in guarding Chicheng and Dushi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hong was ordered to assist Vice Commander Li Qian in guarding Chicheng and Dushi.

sentences.zh: 謙老而怯，故與洪左。

translations.literal: Qian was old and timid, and therefore was paired with Hong on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was old and timid, so Hong was assigned to serve alongside him.

sentences.zh: 洪每調軍，謙輒陰沮之。

translations.literal: Whenever Hong mustered troops, Qian would secretly obstruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Hong mustered troops, Qian would secretly obstruct him.

sentences.zh: 洪嘗勵將士殺敵，謙笑曰：「敵可盡乎？

translations.literal: Hong once exhorted the officers and men to kill the enemy; Qian laughed and said: "Can the enemy be exhausted?
translations.idiomatic: Once, when Hong urged his officers and men to kill the enemy, Qian laughed and said, "Can you ever exhaust the enemy?

sentences.zh: 徒殺吾人耳。

translations.literal: You will only kill our own men."
translations.idiomatic: You will only get our own men killed."

sentences.zh: 」御史張鵬劾罷謙，因命洪代，洪益自奮。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Peng impeached and removed Qian, and Hong was ordered to replace him; Hong strove all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Peng impeached Qian and had him removed; Hong was put in his place and threw himself into the work with renewed energy.

sentences.zh: 朝廷亦厚待之，每奏捷，功雖微必敘。

translations.literal: The court also treated him generously: whenever he reported victory, even slight merit was recorded in rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The court treated him generously as well: whenever he reported a victory, even a minor exploit was entered in the record of rewards.

sentences.zh: 洪初敗兀良哈兵，執其部長朵欒帖木兒。

translations.literal: Hong first defeated Uriankhai troops and captured their chief Duoluo Timur.
translations.idiomatic: Hong first defeated the Uriankhai and captured their chief Duoluo Timur.

sentences.zh: 既代謙任，復敗其兵於西涼亭。

translations.literal: After he replaced Qian in the post, he again defeated their troops at Xiliang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After replacing Qian in command, he defeated them again at Xiliang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 帝賜敕嘉獎。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 又敕宣大總兵官譚廣等曰：「此即前寇延綏，為指揮王禎所敗者，去若軍甚邇，顧不能撲滅，若視洪等愧不？

translations.literal: He also instructed the Commander-in-Chief of Xuanfu and Datong, Tan Guang, and others: "These are the very raiders who earlier troubled Yan-sui and were defeated by Commander Wang Zhen; they are very near your armies, yet you could not wipe them out—are you not ashamed when you look at Hong and the like?"
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Tan Guang, commander-in-chief of Xuanfu and Datong, and others: "These are the same raiders who earlier harried Yan-sui and were beaten by Commander Wang Zhen. They were right beside your armies, yet you could not destroy them—do you not feel ashamed when you compare yourselves with men like Hong?"

sentences.zh: 」三年春，擊寇於伯顏山。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he struck the raiders at Bayan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he attacked the raiders at Bayan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 洪馬蹶傷足，戰益力，擒其部長也陵臺等四人。

translations.literal: Hong's horse stumbled and injured his foot, yet he fought all the harder and captured their chiefs Yelintai and three others.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's horse stumbled and injured his foot, yet he fought all the harder and captured four of their chiefs, including Yelintai.

sentences.zh: 追至寶昌州，又擒阿臺答剌花等五人。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Baochang Prefecture, he again captured Atai Dalihua and five others.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing as far as Baochang Prefecture, he captured five more men, including Atai Dalihua.

sentences.zh: 寇大敗，遁去。

translations.literal: The raiders were badly defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders were routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 璽書慰勞，遣醫視，進都指揮同知，賜銀幣。

translations.literal: An imperial letter comforted and rewarded him; a physician was sent to attend him; he was promoted to Vice Commander-in-Chief and given silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a letter of consolation, dispatched a physician to treat him, promoted him to Vice Commander-in-Chief, and granted him silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 尋以譚廣老，命充右參將佐之。

translations.literal: Soon, because Tan Guang was old, he was ordered to serve as Right Assistant Commander to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because Tan Guang was aging, Hong was appointed Right Assistant Commander to assist him.

sentences.zh: 洪建議加築開平城，拓龍門所，自獨石至潮河川，增置堠臺六十。

translations.literal: Hong proposed adding fortifications to Kaiping city, expanding Longmen post, and from Dushi to Chaohe River adding sixty beacon towers.
translations.idiomatic: Hong proposed strengthening the walls of Kaiping, expanding Longmen post, and building sixty beacon towers from Dushi to the Chaohe River.

sentences.zh: 尋進都指揮使。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 與兀良哈兵戰三岔口。

translations.literal: He fought Uriankhai troops at Sanchakou.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the Uriankhai at Sanchakou.

sentences.zh: 又嘗追寇至亦把禿河。

translations.literal: He also once pursued raiders to the Yibatu River.
translations.idiomatic: He also once pursued raiders as far as the Yibatu River.

sentences.zh: 再遷都督同知。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Vice Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 九年，兀良哈寇延綏，洪與內臣韓政等出大同，至黑山迤北，邀破之克列蘇。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Uriankhai raided Yan-sui; Hong with the eunuch Han Zheng and others marched out from Datong to north of Heishan and intercepted and defeated them at Keliesu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Uriankhai raided Yan-sui. Hong, the eunuch Han Zheng, and others marched out from Datong, advanced north of Heishan, and intercepted and defeated them at Keliesu.

sentences.zh: 進左都督，軍士蒙賞者九千九百余人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Regional Commander; more than nine thousand nine hundred soldiers received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Regional Commander, and more than nine thousand nine hundred of his soldiers received rewards.

sentences.zh: 洪嘗請給旗牌，不許。

translations.literal: Hong once requested the issue of command flags and tablets; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Hong once asked for command flags and tablets, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 乃自制小羽箭、木牌令軍中。

translations.literal: He then made his own small feathered arrows and wooden tokens and imposed them on the army.
translations.idiomatic: He then devised his own small signal arrows and wooden tokens for use in the army.

sentences.zh: 有司論其專擅，帝不問。

translations.literal: The responsible officials charged him with usurpation of authority; the emperor did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials accused him of overstepping his authority, but the emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 十二年充總兵官，代郭竑鎮宣府。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was made Commander-in-Chief, replacing Guo Cong to command Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed Commander-in-Chief, replacing Guo Cong as commander of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 自宣德以來，迤北未嘗大舉入寇。

translations.literal: Since the Xuande reign the northern frontier had not seen a major invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xuande reign the northern frontier had not suffered a major invasion.

sentences.zh: 惟朵顏三衛眾乘間擾邊，多不過百騎，或數十騎。

translations.literal: Only the masses of the Three Guards of Doyin took opportunities to harass the border, usually no more than a hundred horsemen, or several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Three Guards of Doyin took advantage of openings to raid the border, usually with no more than a hundred horsemen, sometimes only a few dozen.

sentences.zh: 他將率巽軿，洪獨以敢戰至大將。

translations.literal: Other generals for the most part were compliant and timid; Hong alone, through daring in battle, rose to great commander.
translations.idiomatic: Other generals were for the most part timid and compliant, but Hong alone rose to high command through his boldness in battle.

sentences.zh: 諸部亦憚之，稱為「楊王」。

translations.literal: The various tribes also feared him and called him "Prince Yang."
translations.idiomatic: The frontier tribes feared him as well and called him "Prince Yang."

sentences.zh: 瓦剌可汗脫脫不花、太師也先皆嘗致書於洪，並遺之馬。

translations.literal: The Oirat khan Togto Buqa and Grand Preceptor Esen had both sent letters to Hong and presented him with horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Oirat khan Togto Buqa and Grand Preceptor Esen had both written to Hong and sent him horses as gifts.

sentences.zh: 洪聞於朝，敕令受之而報以禮。

translations.literal: Hong reported to court; an edict ordered him to accept and reply with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Hong reported this to court, and was ordered to accept the gifts and respond with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 嗣後數有贈遺，帝方倚任洪，不責也。

translations.literal: Afterward there were repeated gifts; the emperor was then relying on Hong and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: There were repeated gifts afterward, but the emperor was then relying heavily on Hong and did not reproach him.

sentences.zh: 帝既北狩，道宣府，也先傳帝命趣開門。

translations.literal: After the emperor had been taken north on campaign, passing Xuanfu, Esen conveyed the emperor's order to hurry and open the gate.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor had been carried off on the northern campaign and passed through Xuanfu, Esen relayed the emperor's order to open the gates at once.

sentences.zh: 城上人對曰：「所守者主上城池。

translations.literal: Those atop the wall answered: "What we guard is our lord's city.
translations.idiomatic: Those on the wall answered, "What we guard is our sovereign's city.

sentences.zh: 天已暮，門不敢開。

translations.literal: Heaven is already dark; we dare not open the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Night has fallen, and we dare not open the gate.

sentences.zh: 且洪已他往。

translations.literal: Moreover Hong has already gone elsewhere."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Hong is already elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 」也先乃擁帝去。

translations.literal: Esen then led the emperor away.
translations.idiomatic: Esen then led the captive emperor away.

sentences.zh: 景帝監國，論前後功，封昌平伯。

translations.literal: When the Jing Emperor acted as regent, his earlier and later merits were weighed and he was enfeoffed as Baron of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing Emperor was regent, Hong's services before and after were weighed and he was enfeoffed as Baron of Changping.

sentences.zh: 也先復令帝為書遺洪，洪封上之。

translations.literal: Esen again had the emperor write a letter to send to Hong; Hong sealed it and forwarded it upward.
translations.idiomatic: Esen again had the captive emperor write to Hong; Hong sealed the letter and forwarded it to court.

sentences.zh: 時景帝已即位，馳使報洪：「上皇書，偽也。

translations.literal: The Jing Emperor had already taken the throne; a fast messenger reported to Hong: "Letters from the Retired Emperor are forged.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Jing Emperor had already ascended the throne and sent a fast courier to tell Hong, "Any letter from the Retired Emperor is a forgery.

sentences.zh: 自今雖真書，毋受。

translations.literal: From now on, even if genuine, do not accept them."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, even if a letter is genuine, you are not to accept it."

sentences.zh: 」於是洪一意堅守。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hong devoted himself single-mindedly to holding firm.
translations.idiomatic: Hong thereupon resolved to hold the frontier without compromise.

sentences.zh: 也先逼京師，急詔洪將兵二萬入衛。

translations.literal: Esen pressed on the capital; an urgent edict ordered Hong to lead twenty thousand troops to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen pressed on the capital, an urgent edict ordered Hong to lead twenty thousand men to its defense.

sentences.zh: 比至，寇已退。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, the raiders had already withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, the raiders had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 敕洪與孫鏜、範廣等追擊余寇。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hong, with Sun Tang, Fan Guang, and others, to pursue the remaining raiders.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Hong, together with Sun Tang, Fan Guang, and others, to pursue the remaining raiders.

sentences.zh: 至霸州破之，獲阿歸等四十八人，還所掠人畜萬計。

translations.literal: Reaching Bazhou he defeated them, captured Agui and forty-eight others, and recovered tens of thousands of people and livestock that had been seized.
translations.idiomatic: At Bazhou he routed them, captured forty-eight men including Agui, and recovered tens of thousands of people and livestock that had been carried off.

sentences.zh: 及關，寇返鬥，殺官軍數百人，洪子俊幾為所及。

translations.literal: At the pass the raiders turned and fought, killing several hundred government troops; Hong's son Jun was nearly caught.
translations.idiomatic: At the pass the raiders turned and fought back, killing several hundred government troops; Hong's son Jun was nearly caught.

sentences.zh: 寇去，以功進侯，命率所部留京師，督京營訓練，兼掌左府事。

translations.literal: When the raiders departed, for his merit he was advanced to marquis, ordered to lead his command to remain at the capital, supervise training of the capital camps, and concurrently manage affairs of the Left Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After the raiders withdrew he was raised to marquis for his service, ordered to keep his command at the capital, put in charge of training the capital camps, and given concurrent charge of the Left Bureau.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以洪宿將，所言多采納。

translations.literal: The court, because Hong was a veteran general, mostly adopted what he said.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hong was a veteran commander, the court largely adopted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 嘗陳禦寇三策，又奏請簡汰三千諸營將校，不得以貧弱充伍，皆從之。

translations.literal: He once set forth three strategies for repelling raiders, and also memorialized requesting selection and weeding of the three-thousand-man camp officers so that the poor and weak could not fill the ranks; all were followed.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted three strategies for repelling raiders and also memorialized that the officers of the three-thousand-man camps be screened so that the poor and weak could not fill the ranks; the court approved both requests.

sentences.zh: 洪久居宣府，禦兵嚴肅，士馬精強，為一時邊將冠。

translations.literal: Hong long resided at Xuanfu; his control of troops was stern and solemn, men and horses elite and strong, and he was the foremost frontier general of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had long held Xuanfu. His discipline was severe, his men and horses were the finest on the frontier, and for a time no border commander ranked above him.

sentences.zh: 然未嘗專殺，又頗好文學，嘗請建學宣府，教諸將子弟。

translations.literal: Yet he never killed on his own authority, and was rather fond of letters; he once requested establishing a school at Xuanfu to teach the sons of the various generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he never executed anyone on his own authority, and he had a genuine love of learning; he once asked to establish a school at Xuanfu to educate the sons of frontier officers.

sentences.zh: 子傑嗣，上言：「臣家一侯三都督，蒼頭得官者十六人，大懼不足報稱。

translations.literal: His son Jie succeeded and memorialized: "In my household there is one marquis and three regional commanders, and sixteen household servants who have received office; I greatly fear I am unworthy to repay such favor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jie succeeded him and memorialized, "Our household already holds one marquisate and three regional commands, and sixteen household servants have been given office. I fear we can never repay such favor.

sentences.zh: 乞停蒼頭楊釗等職。

translations.literal: I beg that the offices of household servants Yang Zhao and others be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the offices granted to household servants such as Yang Zhao be withdrawn."

sentences.zh: 」詔許之，仍令給俸。

translations.literal: An edict permitted it, but still ordered that salaries be paid.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the request but ordered that their salaries continue to be paid.

sentences.zh: 傑卒，無子，庶兄俊嗣。

translations.literal: Jie died without a son; his elder brother by a concubine, Jun, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie died without an heir, his elder half-brother Jun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 俊，初以舍人從軍。

translations.literal: Jun, at first as a household attendant, followed the army.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had first entered service as a household attendant with the army.

sentences.zh: 正統中累官署都指揮僉事，總督獨石、永寧諸處邊務。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong reign he rose through posts to Acting Assistant Commander-in-Chief and supervised frontier affairs at Dushi, Yongning, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign he rose to Acting Assistant Commander-in-Chief and took charge of frontier affairs at Dushi, Yongning, and neighboring posts.

sentences.zh: 景帝即位，給事中金達奉使獨石，劾俊貪侈，乃召還。

translations.literal: When the Jing Emperor took the throne, Supervising Secretary Jin Da, on a mission to Dushi, impeached Jun for greed and extravagance, and he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing Emperor came to the throne, Supervising Secretary Jin Da, on a mission to Dushi, impeached Jun for greed and extravagance, and Jun was recalled.

sentences.zh: 也先犯京師，俊敗其別部於居庸，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: When Esen attacked the capital, Jun defeated a detached force of his at Juyong and was promoted to Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen attacked the capital, Jun defeated one of his detached columns at Juyong and was promoted to Vice Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 尋充右參將，佐朱謙鎮宣府。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Right Assistant Commander to assist Zhu Qian in commanding Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Right Assistant Commander to assist Zhu Qian in commanding Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 太監喜寧數誘敵入寇，中朝患之，購擒斬寧者賞黃金千兩，白金二萬兩，爵封侯。

translations.literal: The eunuch Xi Ning repeatedly lured the enemy to raid; the central court was troubled by this and offered a reward of one thousand taels of gold and twenty thousand taels of silver, with enfeoffment as marquis, to whoever captured and executed Ning.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Xi Ning had repeatedly lured the enemy into raids, to the court's great alarm. A reward of one thousand taels of gold and twenty thousand taels of silver, together with a marquisate, was offered to whoever captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 寧為都指揮江福所獲，而俊冒其功。

translations.literal: Ning was captured by Commander Jiang Fu, but Jun claimed the credit.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was captured by Commander Jiang Fu, but Jun claimed the credit for himself.

sentences.zh: 廷臣請如詔。

translations.literal: Court ministers requested that the edict be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers asked that the promised reward be granted as announced.

sentences.zh: 帝以俊邊將，職所當為，不允。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Jun was a frontier general and this was within the duty of his post, did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, saying that as a frontier commander Jun had merely done his duty.

sentences.zh: 加右都督，賜金幣。

translations.literal: He was made Right Regional Commander and given gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Regional Commander and granted gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 俊恃父勢橫恣，嘗以私憾杖都指揮陶忠至死。

translations.literal: Jun relied on his father's power and acted arrogantly and willfully; once, over a private grudge, he beat Commander Tao Zhong to death with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Jun relied on his father's power and behaved with arrogant license; once, over a private grudge, he beat Commander Tao Zhong to death with a staff.

sentences.zh: 洪懼，奏俊輕躁，恐誤邊事，乞令來京，隨臣操練。

translations.literal: Hong was afraid and memorialized that Jun was rash and impetuous, feared he might mishandle frontier affairs, and begged that he be ordered to the capital to train under Hong's command.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Hong memorialized that Jun was rash and impetuous and might mishandle frontier affairs, and asked that he be summoned to the capital to train under his own command.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 既至，言官交劾，下獄論斬。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, censors impeached him in succession; he was imprisoned and sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived in the capital, censors impeached him in succession, and he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 詔令隨洪立功。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to follow Hong and earn merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to follow Hong and earn merit on campaign.

sentences.zh: 未幾，冒擒喜寧功事覺，詔追奪冒升官軍，別賞福等，而降俊官，令剿賊自效。

translations.literal: Before long the matter of his falsely claiming credit for capturing Xi Ning came to light; an edict ordered the recovery of promotions wrongly granted to soldiers, separate rewards for Fu and others, and a reduction in Jun's rank, with orders to suppress bandits to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his false claim to credit for capturing Xi Ning was exposed. The court ordered promotions wrongly granted to his men revoked, gave separate rewards to Fu and others, reduced Jun's rank, and told him to redeem himself by suppressing bandits.

sentences.zh: 俄充遊擊將軍，巡僥真、保、涿、易諸城，還督三千營訓練。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Mobile General, patrolling the cities of Zhenbao, Baoding, Zhuo, and Yi, and then returned to supervise training of the Three-Thousand-Man Camp.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Mobile General to patrol Zhenbao, Baoding, Zhuo, Yi, and other posts, then put back in charge of training the Three-Thousand-Man Camp.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年，俊上疏曰：「也先既弒其主，並其眾，包藏禍心，窺伺邊境，直須時動耳。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai, Jun memorialized: "Esen has already murdered his lord and absorbed his followers; he harbors evil intent and watches the border—he needs only the right moment to move.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 3, Jun memorialized: "Esen has murdered his lord and absorbed his followers. He harbors hostile intent and watches our border; he needs only the right moment to strike.

sentences.zh: 聞其妻孥輜重去宣府才數百里。

translations.literal: I hear that his wives, children, and baggage train are only a few hundred li from Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that his family and baggage train are only a few hundred li from Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 我緣邊宿兵不下數十萬，宜分為奇正以待，誘使來攻。

translations.literal: Our frontier garrisons number no less than several hundred thousand; we should divide them into regular and surprise forces to wait, and lure the enemy to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Our frontier garrisons number well over a hundred thousand. We should divide them into main and flanking forces, hold ready, and lure the enemy to attack.

sentences.zh: 正兵列營大同、宣府，堅壁觀變，而出奇兵倍道搗其巢。

translations.literal: The regular troops should encamp at Datong and Xuanfu, hold the walls and watch developments, while surprise forces take a rapid route to strike their nest.
translations.idiomatic: The main army should encamp at Datong and Xuanfu, hold the walls, and watch developments, while a flanking force takes a rapid route to strike their base.

sentences.zh: 彼必還自救，我軍夾攻，可以得誌。

translations.literal: They will certainly return to save themselves; our armies will attack from both sides and can achieve our aim."
translations.idiomatic: They will certainly hurry back to save themselves, and our armies can attack from both sides and achieve our aim."

sentences.zh: 」疏下廷議，于謙等以計非萬全，遂寢。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down for court discussion; Yu Qian and others held that the plan was not fully secure, and it was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to court discussion. Yu Qian and others held that the plan was not fully reliable, and it was dropped.

sentences.zh: 團營初設，命俊分督四營。

translations.literal: When the Corps Camps were first established, Jun was ordered to supervise four camps in division.
translations.idiomatic: When the Corps Camps were first established, Jun was put in charge of four of them.

sentences.zh: 明年復充遊擊將軍，送瓦剌使歸。

translations.literal: The next year he again served as Mobile General, escorting Oirat envoys home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again served as Mobile General escorting Oirat envoys home.

sentences.zh: 至永寧，被酒，杖都指揮姚貴八十，且欲斬之。

translations.literal: Reaching Yongning, he was drunk, beat Commander Yao Gui eighty strokes with a staff, and even wished to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongning he was drunk, had Commander Yao Gui beaten eighty strokes with a staff, and even tried to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 諸將力解而止。

translations.literal: The generals strenuously interceded and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals interceded strenuously and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 貴訴於朝，宣府參政葉盛亦論俊罪。

translations.literal: Gui appealed to court; Ye Sheng, administrative commissioner of Xuanfu, also discussed Jun's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Gui appealed to court, and Ye Sheng, administrative commissioner of Xuanfu, also memorialized against Jun.

sentences.zh: 以俊嘗潰於獨石，斥為敗軍之將。

translations.literal: Because Jun had once been routed at Dushi, he was denounced as a defeated general.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jun had once been routed at Dushi, he was denounced as a commander of defeated troops.

sentences.zh: 俊上疏自理，封還所賜敕書，以明己功。

translations.literal: Jun memorialized in his own defense, sealed and returned the edicts he had been given, to make clear his own merit.
translations.idiomatic: Jun memorialized in his own defense, sealed up the edicts that had been granted him, and returned them to make clear his own merit.

sentences.zh: 言官劾其跋扈，論斬，錮之獄。

translations.literal: Censors impeached him for arrogance; he was sentenced to decapitation and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached him for arrogance and license; he was sentenced to death and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 會傑卒，傑母魏氏請暫釋俊營傑葬事。

translations.literal: It happened that Jie died; Jie's mother, the Lady Wei, requested that Jun be temporarily released to arrange Jie's funeral.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Jie died just then. Jie's mother, Lady Wei, asked that Jun be temporarily released to arrange the funeral.

sentences.zh: 乃宥死，降都督僉事。

translations.literal: His death sentence was then spared and he was reduced to Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: His death sentence was commuted and he was reduced to Vice Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 旋襲洪職。

translations.literal: Soon he inherited Hong's post.
translations.idiomatic: He soon inherited Hong's command.

sentences.zh: 家人告俊盜軍儲，再論死，輸贖還爵。

translations.literal: A household member reported that Jun had stolen military stores; he was again sentenced to death, paid a ransom, and recovered his title.
translations.idiomatic: A member of his household reported that he had stolen military stores. He was again sentenced to death, paid a ransom, and recovered his title.

sentences.zh: 久之，又以陰事告俊。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was again reported for secret misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was again reported for secret misconduct.

sentences.zh: 免死奪爵，命其子珍襲。

translations.literal: His death was spared but his title taken; his son Zhen was ordered to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: His life was spared but his title was taken away, and his son Zhen was ordered to inherit in his place.

sentences.zh: 俊初守永寧、懷來，聞也先欲奉上皇還，密戒將士毋輕納。

translations.literal: When Jun first guarded Yongning and Huailai, hearing that Esen wished to send the Retired Emperor back, he secretly warned the officers and men not to receive him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun first held Yongning and Huailai, he heard that Esen meant to send the Retired Emperor back and secretly warned his officers and men not to receive him lightly.

sentences.zh: 既還，又言是將為禍本。

translations.literal: After the emperor returned, he again said that this would be the root of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned, he again said that this would become the root of disaster.

sentences.zh: 及上皇復位，張軏與俊不協，言於朝，遂征下詔獄，坐誅。

translations.literal: When the Retired Emperor regained the throne, Zhang Yuan was at odds with Jun; he spoke in court, and Jun was summoned and imprisoned in the imperial prison, and executed for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: When the Retired Emperor regained the throne, Zhang Yuan, who was at odds with Jun, spoke against him at court. Jun was summoned, imprisoned in the imperial prison, and executed.

sentences.zh: 奪珍爵，戍廣西。

translations.literal: Zhen's title was taken and he was banished to serve in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's title was taken away and he was banished to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，授龍虎衛指揮使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he was made commander of the Longhu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong came to the throne, he was appointed commander of the Longhu Guard.

sentences.zh: 信，字文實。

translations.literal: Xin, style name Wenshi.
translations.idiomatic: Nengxin, styled Wenshi.

sentences.zh: 幼從洪擊敵興州。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Hong to strike the enemy at Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he followed Hong to fight the enemy at Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊將方躍馬出陣前，信直前擒之，以是知名。

translations.literal: An enemy general was just leaping his horse out before the formation; Xin went straight forward and captured him, and thereby became famous.
translations.idiomatic: An enemy commander was leaping his horse out before the line when Xin charged straight ahead and seized him, and thereby made his name.

sentences.zh: 累功至指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he rose to Assistant Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Through repeated exploits he rose to Assistant Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 正統末，進都指揮僉事，守柴溝堡。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengtong he was advanced to Vice Commander-in-Chief and guarded Chaigou Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhengtong reign he was promoted to Vice Commander-in-Chief and put in charge of Chaigou Fort.

sentences.zh: 也先犯京師，入衛，進都指揮同知。

translations.literal: When Esen attacked the capital, he entered to defend it and was advanced to Deputy Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen attacked the capital he marched to its defense and was promoted to Deputy Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 景泰改元，守懷來，寇入不能禦。

translations.literal: When the Jingtai reign began, he guarded Huailai; raiders entered and he could not repel them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingtai reign began he held Huailai, but raiders broke in and he could not repel them.

sentences.zh: 護餉永寧，聞炮聲奔還，皆被劾。

translations.literal: Escorting provisions at Yongning, he heard cannon fire and ran back; for all this he was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: While escorting provisions at Yongning he heard cannon fire and fled back; for these offenses he was impeached.

sentences.zh: 朝議以方用兵，不問。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that troops were then engaged and did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided that because fighting was still under way, the matter would not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 累進都督僉事，代能為左副總兵，協鎮宣府。

translations.literal: He rose through posts to Vice Regional Commander, replaced Neng as Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief, and jointly commanded Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Regional Commander, replaced Neng as Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief, and jointly commanded Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 上言：「鹿角之制，臨陣可捍敵馬，結營可衛士卒，每隊宜置十具。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The deer-antler formation, in battle can repel enemy horses, and in camp can protect soldiers; each company should be provided with ten sets.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The deer-antler formation can repel enemy cavalry in battle and protect troops in camp. Each company should be issued ten sets.

sentences.zh: 遇敵團牌拒前，鹿角列後，神銃弓矢相繼叠發，則守無不固，戰無不克。

translations.literal: When meeting the enemy, round shields should block in front, deer-antlers arrayed behind, and divine guns and bows and arrows fired in succession one upon another—then in defense none will fail to hold firm, and in battle none will fail to conquer."
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy appears, round shields should hold the front, deer-antlers should be arrayed behind, and muskets, bows, and arrows should be fired in succession. Then no defense will fail to hold, and no battle will fail to be won."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 天順初，移鎮延綏，進都督同知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he was transferred to command Yan-sui and advanced to Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign he was transferred to command Yan-sui and promoted to Vice Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 明年破寇青陽溝，大獲。

translations.literal: The next year he defeated raiders at Qingyang Gully with great gain.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he defeated raiders at Qingyang Gully with great success.

sentences.zh: 封彰武伯，佩副將軍印，充總兵官，鎮守如故。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhangwu, wore the seal of Deputy General, and served as Commander-in-Chief with command as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhangwu, given the seal of Deputy General, and appointed Commander-in-Chief with his command unchanged.

sentences.zh: 延綏設總兵官佩印，自信始也。

translations.literal: The establishment at Yan-sui of a Commander-in-Chief bearing a seal began with Xin.
translations.idiomatic: The post of Commander-in-Chief bearing an official seal at Yan-sui began with Xin.

sentences.zh: 頃之，破寇高家堡。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he defeated raiders at Gaojia Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he defeated raiders at Gaojia Fort.

sentences.zh: 三年與石彪大破寇於野馬澗。

translations.literal: In the third year, together with Shi Biao, he inflicted a great defeat on raiders at Yema Ravine.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he and Shi Biao inflicted a major defeat on raiders at Yema Ravine.

sentences.zh: 明年，寇二萬騎入榆林，信擊卻之。

translations.literal: The next year twenty thousand horsemen raided into Yulin; Xin struck and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: The following year twenty thousand horsemen raided into Yulin, and Xin drove them back.

sentences.zh: 追奔至金雞峪，斬平章阿孫帖木兒，還所掠人畜萬計。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rout to Jinjiyu, he beheaded the pingzhang Asun Timur and recovered tens of thousands of people and livestock that had been seized.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the rout as far as Jinjiyu, he killed the pingzhang Asun Timur and recovered tens of thousands of people and livestock that had been carried off.

sentences.zh: 其冬，代李文鎮大同。

translations.literal: That winter he replaced Li Wen in commanding Datong.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he replaced Li Wen as commander of Datong.

sentences.zh: 信在邊三十年，鎮以安靜，人樂為用。

translations.literal: Xin was on the frontier thirty years; he governed with quiet stability and men were glad to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Xin spent thirty years on the frontier. He governed with quiet firmness, and his men were glad to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 然性好營利。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was fond of seeking profit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was fond of profit.

sentences.zh: 代王嘗奏其違法事，詔停一歲祿。

translations.literal: The Prince of Dai once memorialized his illegal acts; an edict suspended his salary for one year.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Dai once memorialized his illegal conduct, and an edict suspended his salary for one year.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬卒於鎮。

translations.literal: In the winter of the thirteenth year he died at his post.
translations.idiomatic: He died at his post in the winter of the thirteenth year.

sentences.zh: 贈侯，謚武毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made marquis, with the posthumous title Martial and Resolute.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as marquis with the posthumous title Martial and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 洪父子兄弟皆佩將印，一門三侯伯。

translations.literal: Hong, his sons, brothers, all wore general's seals; one household held three marquisates and baronies.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, his sons, and his brothers all bore general's seals; one household held three marquisates and baronies.

sentences.zh: 其時稱名將者，推楊氏。

translations.literal: Of those then called famous generals, the Yang clan was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Among the famous generals of the age, the Yang clan stood foremost.

sentences.zh: 昌平侯既廢，能以流爵弗世。

translations.literal: After the Marquisate of Changping was abolished, they were able to hold a flowing title that did not pass by inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: After the Marquisate of Changping was abolished, the family still held a non-hereditary noble title.

sentences.zh: 而信獨傳其子瑾，弘治初領將軍宿衛。

translations.literal: Xin alone passed his title to his son Jin; at the beginning of Hongzhi he led the general's palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xin alone passed his line to his son Jin, who early in the Hongzhi reign commanded the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 三傳至曾孫炳。

translations.literal: Through three generations it passed to his great-grandson Bing.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed through three generations to his great-grandson Bing.

sentences.zh: 隆慶時，協守南京。

translations.literal: In the Longqing reign he jointly guarded Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing reign he helped guard Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 召掌京營戎政，屢加少師。

translations.literal: He was summoned to manage the military administration of the capital camps and was repeatedly given the title of Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to manage the military administration of the capital camps and was repeatedly promoted to Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚恭襄。

translations.literal: He died, with the posthumous title Respectful and Assisting.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Respectful and Assisting.

sentences.zh: 傳子至孫崇猷。

translations.literal: The line passed to his son and on to his grandson Chongyou.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed to his son and then to his grandson Chongyou.

sentences.zh: 李自成陷京師，被殺。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng took the capital, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng took the capital, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 石亨，渭南人。

translations.literal: Shi Heng was a native of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng was from Weinan.

sentences.zh: 生有異狀，方面偉軀，美髯及膝。

translations.literal: At birth he had an unusual appearance: a square face, a grand body, and a fine beard reaching to his knees.
translations.idiomatic: He was born with an unusual appearance: a square face, a powerful frame, and a fine beard that reached his knees.

sentences.zh: 其從子彪魁梧似之，須亦過腹。

translations.literal: His nephew Biao was similarly imposing in stature, and his beard also passed his belly.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Biao was similarly imposing, and his beard also reached past his belly.

sentences.zh: 就飲酒肆，相者曰：「今平也，二人何乃有封侯相？

translations.literal: Once at a wine shop, a physiognomist said: "The realm is at peace now—why do these two have the look of enfeoffment as marquis?"
translations.idiomatic: Once at a wine shop a physiognomist said, "The realm is at peace now—why do these two have the bearing of men destined for enfeoffment?"

sentences.zh: 」亨嗣世父職，為寬河衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Heng succeeded to his uncle's hereditary post and became Assistant Commander of Kuanhe Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Heng inherited his uncle's hereditary post and became Assistant Commander of Kuanhe Guard.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，能用大刀，每戰輒摧破。

translations.literal: He was skilled at mounted archery and could use the great sword; in every battle he would break through.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in horsemanship and archery and adept with the great sword, he broke through the enemy line in every battle.

sentences.zh: 正統初，以獲首功，累遷都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong, for merit in taking heads he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengtong reign, rewarded for taking enemy heads, he rose repeatedly to Vice Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 敗敵黃牛坡，獲馬甚眾。

translations.literal: He defeated the enemy at Huangniu Slope and captured a great many horses.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the enemy at Huangniu Slope and captured a great many horses.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，敵三百余騎飲馬黃河，亨追擊至官山下，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, more than three hundred enemy horsemen were watering their horses at the Yellow River; Heng pursued to below Guanshan and killed and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year more than three hundred enemy horsemen were watering their horses at the Yellow River. Heng pursued them to below Guanshan and killed or captured many.

sentences.zh: 進都指揮同知。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Deputy Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Deputy Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 尋充左參將，佐武進伯朱冕守大同。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Left Assistant Commander to assist the Baron of Wujin, Zhu Mian, in guarding Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Left Assistant Commander to assist Zhu Mian, Baron of Wujin, in guarding Datong.

sentences.zh: 六年上言：「邊餉難繼，請分大同左右、玉林、雲川四衛軍，墾凈水坪迤西曠土，官給牛種，可歲增糧萬八千石。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized: "Frontier provisions are hard to sustain; I request that troops of the four guards of Datong Left and Right, Yulin, and Yunchuan be divided to reclaim the vacant land west of Jingshuiping; if the government supplies oxen and seed, grain can be increased by eighteen thousand piculs yearly."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he memorialized: "Frontier provisions are hard to sustain. I ask that troops from the four guards of Datong Left and Right, Yulin, and Yunchuan be assigned to reclaim vacant land west of Jingshuiping. If the government supplies oxen and seed, we can add eighteen thousand piculs of grain each year."

sentences.zh: 」明年又言：「大同西路屯堡，皆臨極邊。

translations.literal: The next year he again said: "The frontier farms and forts on the western route of Datong all lie on the outermost border.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he memorialized again: "The frontier farms and forts on Datong's western route all lie on the outermost border.

sentences.zh: 玉林故城去右衛五十里，與東勝單於城接，水草便利。

translations.literal: The old city of Yulin is fifty li from Right Guard, adjoins the Chanyu City of Dongsheng, and has convenient grass and water.
translations.idiomatic: The old city of Yulin lies fifty li from Right Guard, adjoins the Chanyu City of Dongsheng, and has ample grass and water.

sentences.zh: 請分軍築壘，防護屯種。

translations.literal: I request that troops be divided to build stockades and protect the farming colonies."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that troops be assigned to build stockades and protect the farming colonies."

sentences.zh: 」詔皆允行。

translations.literal: Edicts approved all and ordered them carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts approved both proposals and ordered them carried out.

sentences.zh: 尋以敗敵紅城功，進都指揮使。

translations.literal: Soon, for merit in defeating the enemy at Hongcheng, he was advanced to Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for defeating the enemy at Hongcheng, he was promoted to Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 敵犯延安，追至金山敗之，再遷都督僉事。

translations.literal: When the enemy raided Yan'an, he pursued to Jinshan and defeated them, and was again transferred to Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy raided Yan'an, he pursued them to Jinshan and defeated them, and was promoted again to Vice Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 亨以國制搜將才未廣，請仿漢、唐制，設軍謀宏遠、智識絕倫等科，令人得自陳，試驗擢用，不專保舉。

translations.literal: Heng, because the national system for seeking generals was not broad enough, requested that following the Han and Tang systems, categories such as Far-reaching Military Counsel and Unmatched Intelligence be established, allowing men to present themselves, be tested and selected for appointment, and not rely solely on recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Heng argued that the national system for finding generals was too narrow. He asked that categories such as Far-reaching Military Counsel and Unmatched Intelligence be established on the Han and Tang model, so that men could present themselves, be tested, and be appointed without relying solely on recommendation.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply was approval.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 十四年，與都督僉事馬麟巡僥塞外。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, with Vice Regional Commander Ma Lin he patrolled beyond the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he patrolled beyond the frontier passes with Vice Regional Commander Ma Lin.

sentences.zh: 至箭豁山，敗兀良哈眾，進都督同知。

translations.literal: Reaching Jianhuo Mountain, he defeated the Uriankhai masses and was advanced to Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianhuo Mountain he defeated the Uriankhai and was promoted to Vice Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 是時，邊將智勇者推楊洪，其次則亨。

translations.literal: At that time among frontier generals for wisdom and courage Yang Hong was foremost, and next came Heng.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Hong was regarded as the foremost frontier commander for wisdom and courage, with Heng next.

sentences.zh: 亨雖偏將，中朝倚之如大帥，故亨亦盡力。

translations.literal: Although Heng was only a subordinate general, the central court relied on him as on a supreme commander, and therefore Heng also exerted himself fully.
translations.idiomatic: Though only a subordinate commander, Heng was relied on at court like a supreme commander, and he in turn gave his full effort.

sentences.zh: 其秋，也先大舉寇大同，亨及西寧侯宋瑛、武進伯朱冕等戰陽和口。

translations.literal: That autumn Esen launched a major raid on Datong; Heng, together with the Marquis of Xining, Song Ying, the Baron of Wujin, Zhu Mian, and others fought at Yanghekou.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Esen launched a major raid on Datong. Heng, together with Song Ying, Marquis of Xining, Zhu Mian, Baron of Wujin, and others fought at Yanghekou.

sentences.zh: 瑛、冕戰沒，亨單騎奔還。

translations.literal: Ying and Mian died in battle; Heng fled back alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Ying and Mian were killed in battle, and Heng fled back alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 降官，募兵自效。

translations.literal: He was demoted in rank and ordered to raise troops to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted and ordered to raise troops and redeem himself through service.

sentences.zh: 郕王監國，尚書于謙薦之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Cheng acted as regent, Minister Yu Qian recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Cheng was regent, Minister Yu Qian recommended him.

sentences.zh: 召掌五軍大營，進右都督。

translations.literal: He was summoned to command the Great Camp of the Five Armies and advanced to Right Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to command the Great Camp of the Five Armies and promoted to Right Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 無何，封武清伯。

translations.literal: Before long he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wuqing.

sentences.zh: 也先逼京師，命偕都督陶瑾等九將，分兵營九門外。

translations.literal: When Esen pressed upon the capital, he was ordered together with Regional Commander Tao Jin and eight other generals to divide troops and encamp outside the nine gates.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen threatened Beijing, Heng was ordered to join Regional Commander Tao Jin and eight other generals in dividing their forces to camp outside the nine city gates.

sentences.zh: 德勝門當敵沖，特以命亨。

translations.literal: Desheng Gate faced the enemy's main thrust; Heng alone was specially assigned there.
translations.idiomatic: As Desheng Gate lay in the path of the main enemy assault, Heng alone was assigned to defend it.

sentences.zh: 于謙以尚書督軍。

translations.literal: Yu Qian, as Minister, supervised the army.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yu Qian directed military affairs.

sentences.zh: 寇薄彰義門，都督高禮等卻之。

translations.literal: The raiders pressed Zhangyi Gate; Regional Commander Gao Li and others repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy pressed Zhangyi Gate, but Regional Commander Gao Li and others drove them back.

sentences.zh: 轉至德勝門外，亨用謙令，伏兵誘擊，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: They then shifted to outside Desheng Gate; Heng, using Yu Qian's order, set an ambush to lure and strike; the dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then moved to Desheng Gate, where Heng, acting on Yu Qian's orders, laid an ambush and lured them into attack, killing a great many.

sentences.zh: 既而圍孫鏜西直門外，以亨救引卻。

translations.literal: Shortly after, they besieged Sun Tang outside Xizhi Gate; through Heng's rescue he drew them back and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They then besieged Sun Tang outside Xizhi Gate, but Heng's relief force drew the enemy off and compelled their withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 相持五日，寇斂眾遁。

translations.literal: They faced each other five days; the raiders gathered their forces and fled.
translations.idiomatic: After five days of stalemate, the raiders gathered their forces and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 論功，亨為多，進侯。

translations.literal: In discussing merit, Heng's was the greatest; he was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When merits were assessed, Heng's contributions ranked highest, and he was promoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年二月命佩鎮朔大將軍印，帥京軍三萬人，巡哨大同。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Jingtai he was ordered to wear the seal of the Grand General Who Pacifies the North, leading thirty thousand capital troops on patrol at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Jingtai 1, he was ordered to bear the seal of Grand General Who Pacifies the North and lead thirty thousand troops from the capital on patrol in the Datong region.

sentences.zh: 遇寇，敗之。

translations.literal: They met raiders and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When they encountered the enemy, they defeated them.

sentences.zh: 其秋，予世襲誥券。

translations.literal: That autumn he was granted a patent of hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he received a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 易儲，加亨太子太師。

translations.literal: The heir was changed; Heng was made Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the succession was changed, Heng was appointed Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 于謙立團營，命亨提督，充總兵官如故。

translations.literal: Yu Qian established the Corps Regiment; Heng was ordered to supervise it, while continuing as Commander-in-Chief as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian established the elite Corps Regiment and put Heng in charge of it, while he continued to serve as overall commander as before.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝將郊，宿齋宮，疾作不能行禮，召亨代。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, as the Emperor was about to perform the suburban sacrifice, he stayed in the fasting palace; illness seized him and he could not perform the rites; Heng was summoned to act in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor was to perform the suburban sacrifice and lodged in the fasting palace, but illness struck and he could not carry out the ceremony, so Heng was summoned to substitute for him.

sentences.zh: 亨受命榻前，見帝病甚，遂與張軏、曹吉祥等謀迎立上皇。

translations.literal: Heng received the command before the couch; seeing the Emperor's illness was severe, he then with Zhang Yue, Cao Jixiang, and others plotted to welcome and establish the Former Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Heng accepted orders at the emperor's bedside; seeing how gravely ill the emperor was, he joined Zhang Yue, Cao Jixiang, and others in plotting to restore the Former Emperor to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上皇既復辟，以亨首功，進爵忠國公。

translations.literal: Once the Former Emperor had been restored, because Heng was credited with the foremost merit, he was advanced in rank to Duke of Loyalty to the State.
translations.idiomatic: After the Former Emperor's restoration, Heng was credited as the chief architect of the coup and enfeoffed as Duke of Loyal States.

sentences.zh: 眷顧特異，言無不從。

translations.literal: Favor and regard were exceptionally singular; in speech nothing was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed him extraordinary favor, and nothing he said went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 其弟侄家人冒功錦衣者五十余人，部曲親故竄名「奪門」籍得官者四千余人。

translations.literal: His younger brothers, nephews, and household retainers who falsely claimed merit as Embroidered Guards numbered more than fifty; personal troops and kin who slipped their names onto the "Restoring the Throne" register to gain office numbered more than four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty of his brothers, nephews, and retainers falsely claimed merit as Embroidered Guards, and more than four thousand followers and clients gained office by adding their names to the "Restoring the Throne" roll.

sentences.zh: 兩京大臣，斥逐殆盡。

translations.literal: Great ministers of both capitals were expelled and driven out, nearly to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Virtually all the senior ministers of both capitals were driven from office.

sentences.zh: 納私人重賄，引用太仆丞孫弘，郎中陳汝言、蕭璁、張用瀚、郝璜、龍文、朱銓，員外郎劉本道為侍郎。

translations.literal: Taking bribes from private persons, he promoted Grand Transport Assistant Sun Hong, Directors Chen Ruyan, Xiao Cong, Zhang Yonghan, Hao Huang, Long Wen, Zhu Quan, and Assistant Director Liu Bendao to Vice Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted hefty bribes from private parties and promoted Sun Hong, Chen Ruyan, Xiao Cong, Zhang Yonghan, Hao Huang, Long Wen, Zhu Quan, and Liu Bendao to vice-ministerial posts.

sentences.zh: 時有語曰「朱三千，龍八百」。

translations.literal: At the time there was a saying: "Zhu three thousand, Long eight hundred."
translations.idiomatic: A popular saying at the time ran: "Zhu at three thousand, Long at eight hundred."

sentences.zh: 勢焰熏灼，嗜進者競走其門。

translations.literal: His blazing authority scorched; those eager for advancement raced to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: His power blazed so brightly that office-seekers thronged his gate.

sentences.zh: 既以私憾殺于謙、範廣等，又以給事中成章、御史甘澤等九人嘗攻其失，貶黜之。

translations.literal: Having already killed Yu Qian, Fan Guang, and others out of private resentment, he also demoted and banished nine men including Supervising Secretary Zhang Cheng and Censor Gan Ze, who had once attacked his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Having already killed Yu Qian, Fan Guang, and others out of private spite, he also demoted Supervising Secretary Zhang Cheng, Censor Gan Ze, and seven others who had previously censured him.

sentences.zh: 數興大獄，構陷耿九疇、嶽正，而戍楊瑄、張鵬，謫周斌、盛颙等。

translations.literal: He repeatedly raised great prosecutions, framed Geng Jiuchou and Yue Zheng, and sent Yang Xuan and Zhang Peng to border garrison while banishing Zhou Bin, Sheng Yong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly instigated major trials, framed Geng Jiuchou and Yue Zheng, sent Yang Xuan and Zhang Peng into exile on the frontier, and banished Zhou Bin, Sheng Yong, and others.

sentences.zh: 又惡文臣為巡撫，抑武臣不得肆，盡撤還。

translations.literal: He also hated that civil officials served as grand coordinators, which kept military men from acting freely, and had them all recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He also resented civil grand coordinators, who restrained military officers, and had them all recalled.

sentences.zh: 由是大權悉歸亨。

translations.literal: By this, great power entirely returned to Heng.
translations.idiomatic: From this point nearly all real authority rested with Heng.

sentences.zh: 亨無日不進見，數預政事。

translations.literal: Heng had no day on which he did not advance in audience; he frequently participated in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Heng saw the emperor every day and regularly intervened in policy.

sentences.zh: 所請或不從，艴然見於辭色。

translations.literal: When what he requested was sometimes not followed, anger plainly showed in his words and expression.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sometimes refused his requests, he showed his displeasure openly in word and face.

sentences.zh: 即不召，必假事以入，出則張大其勢，市權利。

translations.literal: Even when not summoned, he was sure to enter on some pretext; going out he magnified his power and marketed profit and influence.
translations.idiomatic: Even without a summons he found some excuse to enter the palace; once outside he flaunted his power and traded in influence and profit.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝不能堪，嘗以語閣臣李賢。

translations.literal: After a long time the Emperor could not bear it and once spoke of this to Grand Secretary Li Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In time the emperor could endure it no longer and once confided as much to Grand Secretary Li Xian.

sentences.zh: 賢曰：「惟獨斷乃可。

translations.literal: Xian said: "Only independent decision can do it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian said, "Your Majesty can overcome this only by decisive action of your own."

sentences.zh: 」帝然之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark in source. The Emperor assented to this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 一日語賢曰：「閣臣有事，須燕見。

translations.literal: One day he said to Xian: "Grand secretaries have business and must be received at informal audience.
translations.idiomatic: One day he told Li Xian, "When grand secretaries have business they should be received in private audience.

sentences.zh: 彼武臣，何故頻見？

translations.literal: That military man — why does he see me so often?"
translations.idiomatic: Why should that military man be allowed to see me so constantly?"

sentences.zh: 」遂敕左順門，非宣召毋得納總兵官。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark in source. He then ordered the Left Straight Gate: without imperial summons, the Commander-in-Chief must not be admitted.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered that no commander-in-chief might enter through the Left Straight Gate without being expressly summoned.

sentences.zh: 亨自此稀燕見。

translations.literal: From this Heng rarely had informal audience.
translations.idiomatic: After this Heng was rarely admitted to private audience.

sentences.zh: 亨嘗白帝立碑於其祖墓。

translations.literal: Heng once informed the Emperor to erect a stele at his grandfather's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Heng once petitioned the emperor to erect a memorial stele at his grandfather's grave.

sentences.zh: 工部希亨指，請敕有司建立，翰林院撰文。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Works, courting Heng's wishes, requested an imperial decree for the relevant offices to establish it and the Hanlin Academy to compose the inscription.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Works, eager to please Heng, asked for an imperial order commanding local officials to erect the stele and the Hanlin Academy to draft the text.

sentences.zh: 帝以永樂以來，無為功臣祖宗立碑故事，責部臣，而令亨自立。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because since Yongle there had been no precedent of erecting steles for meritorious officials' ancestors, blamed the ministry officials, and ordered Heng to erect it himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted that since the Yongle reign no precedent existed for such ancestral steles to meritorious officials, rebuked the ministry, and told Heng to erect the monument at his own expense.

sentences.zh: 初，帝命所司為亨營第。

translations.literal: Initially the Emperor had ordered the relevant offices to build a residence for Heng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had earlier ordered officials to build Heng a mansion.

sentences.zh: 既成，壯麗逾制。

translations.literal: When finished, it was magnificent beyond regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When it was completed, its grandeur exceeded what regulations allowed.

sentences.zh: 帝登翔鳳樓見之，問誰所居。

translations.literal: The Emperor ascended the Flying Phoenix Tower and saw it, and asked whose dwelling it was.
translations.idiomatic: From the Flying Phoenix Tower the emperor saw it and asked who lived there.

sentences.zh: 恭順侯吳瑾謬對曰：「此必王府。

translations.literal: Marquis of Gongshun Wu Jin falsely replied: "This must be a princely mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jin, Marquis of Gongshun, answered deceitfully, "That must surely be a prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「非也。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark in source. The Emperor said: "It is not."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "It is not."

sentences.zh: 」瑾曰：「非王府，誰敢僭逾若此？

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark in source. Jin said: "If not a princely mansion, who would dare to overstep thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "If it is not a prince's, who else would dare such presumption?"

sentences.zh: 」帝頷之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark in source. The Emperor nodded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded in assent.

sentences.zh: 亨既權侔人主，而從子彪亦封定遠侯，驕橫如亨。

translations.literal: Heng's power now matched the sovereign's, and his nephew Biao was also enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingyuan, arrogant and overbearing like Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's authority now rivaled the throne's, and his nephew Biao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingyuan, no less arrogant than Heng himself.

sentences.zh: 兩家蓄材官猛士數萬，中外將帥半出其門。

translations.literal: The two households stored warrior officers and fierce soldiers numbering tens of thousands; within and without, generals and commanders half came from their gates.
translations.idiomatic: Between the two households they maintained tens of thousands of fighting men, and half the empire's field commanders owed their posts to their patronage.

sentences.zh: 都人側目。

translations.literal: The capital people looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the capital looked on in fear and resentment.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，彪謀鎮大同，令千戶楊斌等奏保。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year, Biao plotted to take command of Datong and had chiliarch Yang Bin and others memorialize in his favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year Biao schemed to secure command at Datong and had chiliarch Yang Bin and others petition on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝覺其詐，收斌等拷問得實，震怒，下彪詔獄。

translations.literal: The Emperor perceived the fraud, arrested Bin and the others and tortured them until the truth came out, was greatly enraged, and sent Biao to prison by imperial decree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw through the ruse, arrested Yang Bin and his accomplices, and under torture extracted a confession; enraged, he had Biao imprisoned by imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 亨懼，請罪。

translations.literal: Heng was afraid and requested punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was terrified and begged to be punished.

sentences.zh: 帝慰諭之。

translations.literal: The Emperor comforted and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reassured him.

sentences.zh: 亨請盡削弟侄官，放歸田裏。

translations.literal: Heng requested that all his brothers' and nephews' offices be entirely stripped and that they be sent back to the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Heng asked that his brothers' and nephews' offices be stripped and that they be sent home to the countryside.

sentences.zh: 帝亦不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor also did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused even this.

sentences.zh: 及鞫彪，得繡蟒龍衣及違式寢床諸不法事，罪當死。

translations.literal: When Biao was further interrogated, embroidered python-dragon robes were found and an unlawful bed of non-regulation form, among other illegal matters; the crime deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: Further investigation of Biao uncovered python-dragon robes and other regalia, plus a bed of illegal design—offenses punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 遂籍彪家，命亨養病。

translations.literal: Biao's household goods were then confiscated, and Heng was ordered to nurse his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Biao's property was confiscated and Heng was ordered to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 亨嘗遣京衛指揮裴瑄出關市木，遣大同指揮盧昭追捕亡者。

translations.literal: Heng had once sent Capital Guard Commander Pei Xuan beyond the passes to buy timber in the market, and sent Datong Commander Lu Zhao to pursue fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Heng had earlier sent Capital Guard Commander Pei Xuan beyond the frontier to purchase timber and Datong Commander Lu Zhao to hunt down deserters.

sentences.zh: 至是事覺，法司請罪亨，帝猶置不問。

translations.literal: Now the matter came to light; the judicial offices requested punishment for Heng, but the Emperor still set it aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When these abuses came to light the judiciary sought to punish Heng, but the emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 法司再鞫彪，言彪初為大同遊擊，以代王增祿為己功，王至跪謝。

translations.literal: The judiciary interrogated Biao again, saying that Biao had first served as roaming-attacks commander at Datong and claimed as his own merit the Prince of Dai's increased stipend; when the prince came he knelt in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: On re-examining Biao, officials reported that as roaming commander at Datong he had claimed credit for securing an increased stipend for the Prince of Dai, who then came in person to kneel and thank him.

sentences.zh: 自是數款彪，出歌妓行酒。

translations.literal: From this he repeatedly entertained Biao, setting out singing girls to pour wine.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the prince repeatedly hosted Biao and sent out singing girls to serve wine.

sentences.zh: 彪淩侮親王，罪亦當死。

translations.literal: Biao insulted and humiliated the imperial prince; this crime also deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had moreover humiliated a reigning prince, another capital offense.

sentences.zh: 因劾亨招權納賕，肆行無忌，與術士鄒叔彜等私講天文，妄談休咎，宜置重典。

translations.literal: They therefore impeached Heng for monopolizing power and taking bribes, acting without restraint, and for privately discussing astronomy with the technician Zou Shuyi and others, recklessly speaking of good and ill fortune—they should be punished by heavy statute.
translations.idiomatic: The prosecutors therefore charged Heng with grasping power, taking bribes, and consulting fortune-tellers such as Zou Shuyi on celestial signs—offenses warranting the severest penalties.

sentences.zh: 帝命錮彪於獄，亨閑住，罷朝參。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Biao confined in prison, Heng to live in retirement, and court attendance suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Biao imprisoned, confined Heng at home, and barred him from court.

sentences.zh: 時方議革「奪門」功，窮治亨黨，由亨得官者悉黜，朝署一清。

translations.literal: At that time they were just discussing abolishing "Restoring the Throne" merit, prosecuting Heng's faction to the end; those who had gained office through Heng were all dismissed, and the court administration was once made clear.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then revising awards from the "Restoring the Throne" coup and rooting out Heng's faction; everyone who had gained office through him was removed, and for a time the bureaucracy was cleansed.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，錦衣指揮逯杲奏亨怨望，與其從孫後等造妖言，蓄養無賴，專伺朝廷動靜，不軌跡已著。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, Embroidered Guard Commander Lu Gao memorialized that Heng harbored resentment and, with his distant nephew Hou and others, fabricated seditious talk, kept and nourished ruffians, and solely watched the court's movements; traces of disloyalty were already clear.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the first month, Embroidered Guard Commander Lu Gao reported that Heng nursed resentment, that with his grandnephew Hou and others he spread seditious rumors, maintained a band of thugs, and spied on court affairs—clear signs of treason.

sentences.zh: 廷臣皆言不可輕宥。

translations.literal: Court ministers all said he could not be lightly pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers unanimously urged that he not be treated leniently.

sentences.zh: 乃下亨詔獄，坐謀叛律斬，沒其家貲。

translations.literal: Heng was then sent to prison by imperial decree; sentenced under the statute for plotting rebellion, he was to be beheaded, and his household property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was imprisoned, convicted of treason, and sentenced to decapitation with confiscation of his property.

sentences.zh: 逾月，亨瘐死，彪、後並伏誅。

translations.literal: After a month Heng died of illness in confinement; Biao and Hou were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Heng died in prison; Biao and Hou were also put to death.

sentences.zh: 彪驍勇敢戰，善用斧。

translations.literal: Biao was fierce and brave in battle and skilled with the battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: Biao fought with exceptional fierceness and was a master of the battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 初以舍人從軍。

translations.literal: Initially he followed the army as a household guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as a household guardsman in the army.

sentences.zh: 正統末，積功至指揮同知。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengtong he accumulated merit and reached Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Zhengtong reign he had risen to Vice Commander through accumulated merit.

sentences.zh: 也先逼京師，既退，追襲余寇，頗有斬獲，進署都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: When Esen pressed the capital and then withdrew, he pursued and struck the remaining raiders and had considerable beheadings and captures; he was advanced in temporary appointment to Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen threatened Beijing and withdrew, Biao pursued the remnant force, scored notable victories, and was temporarily promoted to Vice Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 景泰改元，詔予實授，充遊擊將軍，守備威遠衛。

translations.literal: When Jingtai changed the reign era, an edict granted him substantive appointment, as roaming-attacks general garrisoning Weiyuan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingtai reign began, he received substantive rank as roaming-attacks general defending Weiyuan Guard.

sentences.zh: 敵圍土城，彪用炮擊死百余人，遁去。

translations.literal: The enemy besieged Tucheng; Biao used cannon fire and killed more than a hundred, and they fled.
translations.idiomatic: When enemies besieged Tucheng, he used artillery to kill more than a hundred men and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 塞上日用兵，彪勇冠流輩，每戰必捷，以故一歲中數遷，至都督僉事。

translations.literal: On the frontier they used troops daily; Biao's courage topped his peers, every battle certain of victory; for this reason within one year he was several times promoted, reaching Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: With constant fighting on the frontier, Biao's valor outshone his peers and he won every engagement, earning several promotions within a single year until he became Vice Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 恃亨勢，多縱家人占民產，又招納流亡五十余戶，擅越關置莊墾田，為給事中李侃、御史張奎所劾，請並罪亨。

translations.literal: Relying on Heng's power, he often let his household seize commoners' property, and also recruited more than fifty fugitives, boldly crossing the frontier to establish estates and open fields; Supervising Secretary Li Kan and Censor Zhang Kui impeached them, requesting that Heng also be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Trading on Heng's influence, he allowed his retainers to seize commoners' lands, sheltered more than fifty fugitives, and illegally opened farms beyond the frontier; Li Kan and Zhang Kui impeached him and demanded that Heng share the blame.

sentences.zh: 景帝皆宥不問，但令給還民產，遣流亡戶復業而已。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingtai all pardoned without inquiry, only ordering that commoners' property be returned and fugitive households sent back to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingtai pardoned them all, merely ordering seized property restored and displaced households returned to lawful work.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，充右參將，協守大同。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year he was appointed Right Vice General to assist in defending Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year he was made Right Vice General to help defend Datong.

sentences.zh: 嘗憾巡撫年富抑己不得逞。

translations.literal: He once resented that Grand Coordinator Nian Fu restrained him and kept him from having his way.
translations.idiomatic: He had long resented Grand Coordinator Nian Fu for checking his abuses.

sentences.zh: 及英宗復辟，召彪還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was restored, Biao was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yingzong's restoration he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 亨方得誌，彪遂誣奏富罪，致之獄。

translations.literal: Heng had just gained his wish; Biao then falsely memorialized charging Fu with crime and had him cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: With Heng ascendant again, Biao fabricated charges against Nian Fu and had him thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進都督同知，再以遊擊將軍赴大同備敵。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to Vice Regional Commander, then again went to Datong as roaming-attacks general to guard against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Vice Regional Commander and returned to Datong as roaming-attacks general to face the northern enemy.

sentences.zh: 與參將張鵬等哨磨兒山。

translations.literal: Together with Vice General Zhang Peng and others he reconnoitered at Mo'er Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Vice General Zhang Peng and others on a reconnaissance mission at Mo'er Mountain.

sentences.zh: 寇千余騎來襲，彪率壯士沖擊，斬把禿王，搴其旗，俘斬百二十人。

translations.literal: More than a thousand enemy horsemen came to attack; Biao led fierce warriors in a charge, beheaded the chieftain Batu Wang, seized his banner, and captured or killed one hundred twenty.
