translations.idiomatic: When more than a thousand enemy horsemen attacked, Biao led a shock charge, killed the chieftain Batu Wang, seized his banner, and took one hundred twenty heads or prisoners.

sentences.zh: 追至三山墩，又斬七十二人。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Sanshan Fort, he beheaded seventy-two more.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued as far as Sanshan Fort and killed seventy-two more.

sentences.zh: 以是封定遠伯，遊擊如故。

translations.literal: For this he was enfeoffed as Baron of Dingyuan, his roaming-attacks command unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was enfeoffed as Baron of Dingyuan while retaining his roaming command.

sentences.zh: 天順二年命偕高陽伯李文赴延綏禦寇，以疾召還，尋充總兵官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshun he was ordered together with Li Wen, Baron of Gaoyang, to go to Yan-sui to repel raiders; recalled on account of illness, he soon took up the post of Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 2 he was sent with Li Wen, Baron of Gaoyang, to Yan-sui to repel invaders; recalled when ill, he soon became overall commander.

sentences.zh: 明年，寇二萬騎入掠安邊營。

translations.literal: The following year, twenty thousand enemy horsemen entered to plunder Anbian Camp.
translations.idiomatic: The next year twenty thousand horsemen crossed in to raid Anbian Camp.

sentences.zh: 彪與彰武伯楊信等禦之，連戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Biao with Yang Xin, Baron of Zhangwu, and others resisted them; battle after battle all were victories.
translations.idiomatic: Biao joined Yang Xin, Baron of Zhangwu, and others in driving them back, winning every engagement.

sentences.zh: 斬鬼力赤，追出塞轉戰六十餘里，生擒四十余人，斬首五百余級，獲馬駝牛羊二萬余，為西北戰功第一。

translations.literal: He beheaded Guilichi, pursued beyond the frontier turning and fighting for more than sixty li, took more than forty alive, beheaded more than five hundred, obtained horses, camels, cattle, and sheep numbering more than twenty thousand — the foremost northwestern battle achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Guilichi, pursued the enemy sixty li beyond the frontier, took more than forty prisoners, claimed over five hundred heads, and seized more than twenty thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep—the greatest victory in the northwest that year.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，進侯。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: On report of the victory he was promoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 彪本以戰功起家，不藉父兄蔭，然一門二公侯，勢盛而驕，多行不義。

translations.literal: Biao had originally risen through battle merit, not relying on father and elder patronage; yet one household held two dukes and marquises, power flourishing yet arrogant, acting much that was unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had won his place by his own sword, without his family's patronage; yet one clan now held two noble titles, and intoxicated by power they committed many wrongs.

sentences.zh: 謀鎮大同，與亨表裏握兵柄，為帝所疑。

translations.literal: Plotting to command Datong, he and Heng outwardly and inwardly grasped military authority, and the Emperor came to suspect them.
translations.idiomatic: His bid to command Datong, coupled with Heng's grip on the army, made the emperor suspect a bid for military dominance.

sentences.zh: 遂及於禍。

translations.literal: Thus he met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he was brought to ruin.

sentences.zh: 後，天順元年進士，助亨籌畫。

translations.literal: Hou, a metropolitan graduate in the first year of Tianshun, assisted Heng in planning.
translations.idiomatic: Hou, who had passed the metropolitan examination in Tianshun 1, had helped Heng plot the restoration.

sentences.zh: 都督杜清出亨門下，後造妖言，有「土木掌兵權」語，蓋言杜也。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Du Qing came from Heng's faction; Hou fabricated seditious talk, with the phrase "Tumu holds military authority" — meaning to point at Du.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Du Qing was a client of Heng's household; Hou spread seditious slogans, including "At Tumu military power is held"—a veiled reference to Du Qing.

sentences.zh: 事覺，後伏誅，清亦流金齒。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, Hou was executed and Qing was also banished to Jinchi.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, Hou was executed and Qing was banished to Jinchi.

sentences.zh: 郭登，字元登，武定侯英孫也。

translations.literal: Guo Deng, style name Yuandeng, was grandson of the Marquis of Wuding, Guo Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Deng, courtesy name Yuandeng, was grandson of Guo Ying, Marquis of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 幼英敏。

translations.literal: In youth he was intelligent and quick.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was exceptionally bright.

sentences.zh: 及長，博聞強記，善議論，好談兵。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he had broad learning and strong memory, was skilled at discourse, and loved to discuss warfare.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he became widely read with a prodigious memory, excelled in debate, and was ever eager to talk strategy.

sentences.zh: 洪熙時，授勛衛。

translations.literal: In the Hongxi reign he was granted appointment as guard of merit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongxi reign he was appointed to the honor guard.

sentences.zh: 正統中，從王驥征麓川有功，擢錦衣衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong reign he followed Wang Ji on the Luchuan campaign with merit, and was promoted to Assistant Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengtong era he served under Wang Ji in the Luchuan campaign, distinguished himself, and was raised to Assistant Commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 又從沐斌征騰沖，遷署都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Again he followed Mu Bin to campaign at Tengchong, and was transferred to acting Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Mu Bin's expedition to Tengchong and was appointed acting Vice Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 十四年，車駕北征，扈從至大同，超拜都督僉事，充參將，佐總兵官廣寧伯劉安鎮守。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the imperial carriage went on the northern expedition; he escorted as attendant to Datong, was exceptionally promoted to Vice Regional Commander, served as deputy general, and assisted the commander-in-chief, Liu An, Baron of Guangning, in garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 of the reign he joined the emperor's northern expedition, escorted the court as far as Datong, was promoted by special order to Vice Regional Commander, made deputy general, and assisted Commander-in-Chief Liu An, Baron of Guangning, in holding the city.

sentences.zh: 朱勇等軍覆，倉猝議旋師。

translations.literal: The armies of Zhu Yong and others were destroyed; in haste they debated withdrawing the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Yong's army was annihilated, the court frantically debated a retreat.

sentences.zh: 登告學士曹鼐、張益曰「車駕宜入紫荊關」，王振不從，遂及於敗。

translations.literal: Deng told Academicians Cao Tai and Zhang Yi that "the imperial carriage ought to enter Zijing Pass"; Wang Zhen did not follow this, and thus they met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Deng urged Academicians Cao Tai and Zhang Yi that the emperor should withdraw through Zijing Pass, but Wang Zhen refused—and disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 當是時，大同軍士多戰死，城門晝閉，人心洶洶。

translations.literal: At that time many Datong soldiers had died in battle, the city gates were closed by day, and people's hearts were turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: By then most of Datong's garrison had been killed in battle, the gates stayed shut day and night, and panic spread through the city.

sentences.zh: 登慷慨奮勵，修城堞，繕兵械；

translations.literal: Deng, impassioned and stirring himself to exertion, repaired parapets and mended weapons;
translations.idiomatic: Deng rallied the defenders with passionate energy, rebuilding the walls and arming the troops;

sentences.zh: 拊循士卒，吊死問傷，親為裹創傅藥。

translations.literal: he comforted and soothed the soldiers, condoled the dead and inquired after the wounded, and personally wrapped wounds and applied medicine.
translations.idiomatic: comforted the troops, mourned the dead and tended the wounded, and personally dressed wounds and applied salves.

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾誓與此城共存亡，不令諸君獨死也。

translations.literal: saying: "I vow to live or die together with this city and will not let you gentlemen die alone.
translations.idiomatic: declaring, "I swear to live or die with this city—I will not let you perish alone.

sentences.zh: 」八月，也先擁帝北去，經大同，使袁彬入城索金幣。

translations.literal: " In the eighth month Esen led the Emperor north, passing Datong, and sent Yuan Bin into the city to demand gold and coin.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighth month Esen marched the captive emperor north past Datong and sent Yuan Bin into the city to demand gold and treasure.

sentences.zh: 登閉城門，以飛橋取彬入。

translations.literal: Deng closed the city gates and used a flying bridge to draw Bin inside.
translations.idiomatic: Deng kept the gates shut and hauled Bin over the walls on a drawbridge.

sentences.zh: 登與安及侍郎沈固、給事中孫祥、知府霍瑄等出謁，伏地慟哭。

translations.literal: Deng with An and Vice Minister Shen Gu, Supervising Secretary Sun Xiang, Prefect Huo Xuan, and others went out to pay homage, prostrating themselves and weeping bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Deng, Liu An, Vice Minister Shen Gu, Supervising Secretary Sun Xiang, Prefect Huo Xuan, and others went out to receive the emperor, prostrating themselves in bitter grief.

sentences.zh: 以金二萬余及宋瑛、朱冕、內臣郭敬家資進帝，以賜也先等。

translations.literal: With more than twenty thousand in gold and the household assets of Song Ying, Zhu Mian, and the eunuch Guo Jing they presented to the Emperor to be bestowed on Esen and others.
translations.idiomatic: They gathered more than twenty thousand taels of gold plus the estates of Song Ying, Zhu Mian, and the eunuch Guo Jing for the emperor to give Esen and his men.

sentences.zh: 是夕，敵營城西。

translations.literal: That night the enemy encamped west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Mongols pitched camp west of the walls.

sentences.zh: 登謀遣壯士劫營迎駕，不果。

translations.literal: Deng plotted to send brave men to raid the camp and welcome back the imperial carriage; it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Deng planned a night raid to rescue the emperor, but the attempt failed.

sentences.zh: 明日，也先擁帝去。

translations.literal: The next day Esen led the Emperor away.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Esen marched the emperor away.

sentences.zh: 景帝監國，進都督同知，充副總兵。

translations.literal: When the Jing Emperor oversaw the realm, Deng was advanced to Vice Regional Commander and served as deputy commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: While the Jing Emperor governed as regent, Deng was promoted to Vice Regional Commander and made deputy commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋令代安為總兵官。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to replace An as commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed to replace Liu An as overall commander.

sentences.zh: 十月，也先犯京師，登將率所部入援，先馳蠟書奏。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Esen attacked the capital; Deng was about to lead his forces to the rescue and first sent an urgent memorial sealed in wax.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen attacked the capital that October, Deng mustered his troops to relieve the city and dispatched an urgent sealed dispatch ahead.

sentences.zh: 奏至，敵已退。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the enemy had already withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: By the time his message reached court, the invaders had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 景帝優詔褒答，進右都督。

translations.literal: The Jing Emperor sent a gracious edict in praise and answer, and advanced him to Right Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing Emperor answered with a gracious edict of praise and promoted him to Right Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 登計京兵新集，不可輕用，上用兵方略十余事。

translations.literal: Deng judged that the capital troops were newly assembled and could not be lightly used, and presented more than ten items of strategy on troop employment to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He argued the newly assembled capital army was not battle-ready and submitted more than a dozen proposals on how the throne should employ its forces.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年春，偵知寇騎數千，自順聖川入營沙窩。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Jingtai, scouts learned that several thousand enemy horsemen had entered from Shunshengchuan and encamped at Shawo.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Jingtai 1 scouts reported several thousand enemy horsemen had entered via Shunsheng River and encamped at Shawo.

sentences.zh: 登率兵躡之，大破其眾，追至栲栳山，斬二百余級，得所掠人畜八百有奇。

translations.literal: Deng led troops in pursuit, greatly defeated their masses, pursued to Kaolao Mountain, beheaded more than two hundred, and recovered more than eight hundred people and livestock that had been plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Deng gave chase, routed them, pursued to Kaolao Mountain, took over two hundred heads, and recovered more than eight hundred captives and stolen livestock.

sentences.zh: 邊將自土木敗後，畏縮無敢與寇戰。

translations.literal: Since the defeat at Tumu, frontier generals had cowered and dared not fight the raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tumu disaster frontier commanders had been too afraid to meet the enemy in the field.

sentences.zh: 登以八百人破敵數千騎，軍氣為之一振，捷聞，封定襄伯，予世券。

translations.literal: Deng with eight hundred men defeated several thousand enemy horsemen; army morale was thereby revived. When victory was reported, he was enfeoffed Baron of Dingxiang and granted an hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: Deng's victory—eight hundred men routing thousands of horsemen—revived the army's spirit; on news of the triumph he was enfeoffed Baron of Dingxiang with a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 四月，寇騎數千奄至，登出東門戰。

translations.literal: In the fourth month several thousand enemy horsemen suddenly arrived; Deng went out the east gate to fight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month thousands of horsemen swept in; Deng met them at the east gate.

sentences.zh: 佯北，誘之入士城。

translations.literal: Feigning retreat north, he lured them into the earthen inner city.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned retreat and lured them into the inner earthen ward.

sentences.zh: 伏起，敵敗走。

translations.literal: Ambushes rose; the enemy were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ambushes sprang up and the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 登度敵且復至，令軍士賫毒酒、羊豕、楮錢，偽為祭冢者，見寇即棄走。

translations.literal: Deng reckoned the enemy would soon return and ordered soldiers to carry poisoned wine, sheep and pigs, and paper money, posing as those sacrificing at tombs; when they saw raiders they cast them down and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Expecting another raid, he had soldiers scatter poisoned wine, meat, and funeral offerings as if mourning at graves, then flee at the enemy's approach.

sentences.zh: 寇至，爭飲食之，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: When raiders arrived, they vied to drink and eat; the dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders seized the bait; a great many died.

sentences.zh: 六月，也先復以二千騎入寇，登再擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Esen again entered to raid with two thousand horsemen; Deng again struck and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Esen returned with two thousand horsemen; Deng drove them off again.

sentences.zh: 越數日，奉上皇至城外，聲言送駕還。

translations.literal: After several days they brought the Former Emperor to outside the walls, proclaiming that they were escorting the imperial carriage back.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Esen brought the captive Former Emperor to the walls, claiming he would return him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 登與同守者設計，具朝服候駕月城內，伏兵城上，俟上皇入，即下月城閘。

translations.literal: Deng and the co-defenders designed a plan: they donned court dress to await the imperial carriage inside the moon-city, stationed ambush troops atop the wall, and waited until the Former Emperor entered, then would lower the moon-city gate.
translations.idiomatic: Deng and the garrison laid a trap: in court robes they waited inside the barbican, with ambush troops above, ready to drop the gate once the Former Emperor entered.

sentences.zh: 也先及門而覺，遂擁上皇去。

translations.literal: Esen reached the gate and perceived this; he then led the Former Emperor away.
translations.idiomatic: Esen sensed the trap at the gate and dragged the Former Emperor away.

sentences.zh: 時鎮守中官陳公忌登。

translations.literal: At that time the garrison eunuch Supervisor Chen Gong bore jealousy toward Deng.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison eunuch Chen Gong had long resented Deng.

sentences.zh: 會有發公奸贓者，公疑登使之，遂與登構。

translations.literal: It happened that someone exposed Gong's treacherous corruption; Gong suspected Deng had set this in motion, and thus he framed Deng.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong's corruption was exposed he blamed Deng and set out to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 帝謂于謙曰：「大同，吾藩籬也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Yu Qian: "Datong is my screen and fence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Yu Qian, "Datong is my frontier bulwark.

sentences.zh: 公與登如是，其何以守！

translations.literal: Gong and Deng are like this — how can it be defended!
translations.idiomatic: With Gong and Deng at each other's throats, how can it be held?

sentences.zh: 」遣右監丞馬慶代公還，登愈感奮。

translations.literal: " He dispatched the Right Assistant Director Ma Qing to replace Gong and recall him; Deng was all the more stirred and inspired.
translations.idiomatic: " He recalled Gong and sent the Right Assistant Director Ma Qing in his place; Deng fought with renewed zeal.

sentences.zh: 初，也先欲取大同為巢穴，故數來攻。

translations.literal: At first Esen had wished to take Datong as a nest and lair, and so came to attack many times.
translations.idiomatic: Esen had wanted Datong as a base and attacked again and again.

sentences.zh: 及每至輒敗，有一營數十人不還者。

translations.literal: Yet each time he arrived he was defeated; there were camps from which dozens did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he was beaten back; sometimes whole squads of dozens never returned.

sentences.zh: 敵氣懾，始有還上皇意。

translations.literal: Enemy spirit was cowed; he then had the intention of returning the Former Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Their morale broke, and Esen began to consider returning the captive emperor.

sentences.zh: 上皇既還，代王仕壥頌登功，乞降敕獎勞。

translations.literal: After the Former Emperor had returned, the Prince of Dai, Shi Zhi, praised Deng's merit and begged that an imperial edict be sent down to reward and console him.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's return, Prince of Dai Shi Zhi praised Deng's service and asked the throne to reward him by edict.

sentences.zh: 兵部言登已封伯，乃止。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War said Deng had already been enfeoffed as baron, and so they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War noted Deng had already been made a baron, and the request was dropped.

sentences.zh: 二年，登以老疾乞休，舉石彪自代，且請令其子嵩宿衛。

translations.literal: In the second year Deng, on account of age and illness, begged to retire, recommended Shi Biao to replace himself, and moreover asked that his son Song be posted to palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he sought retirement on grounds of age and illness, nominated Shi Biao as his successor, and asked that his son Song join the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 帝以嵩為散騎舍人，不聽登辭。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Song a Gentleman-Attendant of the Standard Cavalry but did not heed Deng's resignation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Song to the palace staff but refused Deng's resignation.

sentences.zh: 是時邊患甫息，登悉心措置，思得公廉有為者與俱。

translations.literal: At that time border troubles had just subsided; Deng devoted his heart to arrangements and sought upright, active men to join him.
translations.idiomatic: With the border briefly quiet, Deng threw himself into administration and sought capable, honest men to serve with him.

sentences.zh: 遂劾奏沈固廢事，而薦尚書楊寧、布政使年富。

translations.literal: He then memorialized impeaching Shen Gu for neglecting affairs, and recommended Minister Yang Ning and Provincial Administration Commissioner Nian Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Shen Gu for neglecting his duties and recommended Minister Yang Ning and Administration Commissioner Nian Fu.

sentences.zh: 又言大同既有御史，又有巡按御史，僉都御史任寧宜止巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: He also said that since Datong already had a censor and also a touring-and-inspecting censor, the Vice Censor-in-Chief Ren Ning ought to cease touring and pacifying Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that with both a censor and a touring inspector already at Datong, Vice Censor-in-Chief Ren Ning should confine his patrol to Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 帝悉從之，以年富代固，而征還固及寧。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed all of this, using Nian Fu to replace Gu, and summoning back Gu and Ning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted every recommendation: Nian Fu replaced Shen Gu, and both Shen Gu and Ren Ning were recalled.

sentences.zh: 其秋，以疾召還。

translations.literal: That autumn he was recalled on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn illness brought him back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 登初至大同，士卒可戰者才數百，馬百余匹。

translations.literal: When Deng had first arrived at Datong, soldiers fit for battle were only several hundred, and horses a little more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng first reached Datong, scarcely a few hundred men could fight and only a hundred-odd horses remained.

sentences.zh: 及是馬至萬五千，精卒數萬，屹然成巨鎮。

translations.literal: By this time horses reached fifteen thousand, crack troops numbered tens of thousands, and it stood firm as a great garrison town.
translations.idiomatic: By now he had fifteen thousand horses and tens of thousands of seasoned troops—a fortress in its own right.

sentences.zh: 登去，大同人思之。

translations.literal: When Deng left, the people of Datong thought of him.
translations.idiomatic: When he left, the people of Datong mourned his absence.

sentences.zh: 初，英宗過大同，遣人謂登曰：「朕與登有姻，何拒朕若是？

translations.literal: At first when Emperor Yingzong passed Datong, he sent someone to say to Deng: "I and Deng have marriage kinship — why reject me thus?
translations.idiomatic: Once when Emperor Yingzong passed Datong he sent word: "We are kinsmen by marriage—why shut me out like this?

sentences.zh: 」登奏曰：「臣奉命守城，不知其他。

translations.literal: " Deng memorialized: "Your servant received orders to hold the city and knows nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: " Deng replied in memorial: "I have orders to hold the city and nothing beyond that.

sentences.zh: 」英宗銜之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yingzong bore a grievance against this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor never forgave the rebuff.

sentences.zh: 及復辟，登懼不免，首陳八事，多迎合。

translations.literal: When order was restored, Deng feared he would not escape harm; he first presented eight items, mostly in accommodation.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration he feared execution and led with eight memorial proposals, most of them conciliatory.

sentences.zh: 尋命掌南京中府事。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to manage affairs of the central mansion at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to administer the Nanjing central mansion.

sentences.zh: 明年召還。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 言官劾登結陳汝言獲召，鞫實論斬。

translations.literal: Censorial officials impeached Deng for linking with Chen Ruyan to obtain recall; the truth under interrogation was judged capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Censors charged that Deng had conspired with Chen Ruyan to engineer his recall; investigation found grounds for execution.

sentences.zh: 宥死，降都督僉事，立功甘肅。

translations.literal: His life was spared; he was demoted to Vice Regional Commander and earned merit in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: His life was spared; he was demoted to Vice Regional Commander and sent to win merit on the Gansu frontier.

sentences.zh: 登儀觀甚偉，髯垂過腹。

translations.literal: Deng's bearing and appearance were very grand; his beard hung down past the belly.
translations.idiomatic: He was an imposing figure, his beard falling below his waist.

sentences.zh: 為將兼智勇，紀律嚴明，料敵制勝，動合機宜。

translations.literal: As a general he combined wisdom and courage, his discipline was strict and bright, he estimated the enemy to overcome them, and his movements accorded with opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander he united boldness and craft, enforced iron discipline, read the enemy with uncanny precision, and seized every advantage.

sentences.zh: 嘗以意造「攪地龍」、「飛天網」。

translations.literal: He once according to his own intent fashioned "Earth-Stirring Dragons" and "Sky-Casting Nets."
translations.idiomatic: He devised traps he called the Earth-Stirring Dragon and the Sky-Casting Net.

sentences.zh: 鑿深塹，覆以土木如平地。

translations.literal: He dug deep ditches and covered them with earth and timber like level ground.
translations.idiomatic: He dug deep pits and roofed them with earth and planks so they looked like solid ground.

sentences.zh: 敵入圍中，發其機，自相撞擊，頃刻皆陷。

translations.literal: When the enemy entered and were surrounded within, he released the mechanism; they struck one another, and in an instant all fell in.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy blundered in, he tripped the mechanism; they collapsed into the pits within moments.

sentences.zh: 又仿古制造偏箱車、四輪車，中藏火器，上建旗幟，鉤環聯絡，布列成陣，戰守皆可用。

translations.literal: He also patterned after antiquity in making side-box chariots and four-wheeled chariots, with fire-engines hidden within and banners set atop; hook-rings linked them, arrayed in formation — useful both for battle and for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He also designed antique-style wagons with armored sides and four wheels, each concealing firearms beneath signal banners; linked by hooks into battle lines, they served attack and defense alike.

sentences.zh: 其軍以五人為伍，教之盟於神祠，一人有功，五人同賞，罰亦如之。

translations.literal: His army used five men as one squad; he taught them to covenant at spirit shrines: if one man had merit, five shared reward, and punishment was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: He organized troops in squads of five bound by oath at the shrines—reward or punishment fell on the whole squad.

sentences.zh: 十伍為隊，隊以能挽六十斤弓者為先鋒。

translations.literal: Ten squads made one company; the company took as vanguard one who could draw a sixty-jin bow.
translations.idiomatic: Ten squads formed a company whose vanguard was whoever could draw a sixty-jin bow.

sentences.zh: 十隊領以一都指揮，令功無相撓，罪有專責，一時稱善。

translations.literal: Ten companies were led by one regional commander; merit would not interfere with one another, guilt had dedicated responsibility — for a time all called it good.
translations.idiomatic: Each ten companies reported to a regional commander so credit and blame were clear—an arrangement praised at the time.

sentences.zh: 登事母孝，居喪秉禮。

translations.literal: Deng served his mother with filial piety and observed ritual in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was a devoted son and scrupulous in mourning ritual.

sentences.zh: 能詩，明世武臣無及者。

translations.literal: He could compose poetry; among Ming military officers none reached him.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote verse as well—no martial peer in the dynasty could match him.

sentences.zh: 無子，以兄子嵩為子。

translations.literal: He had no son and took his elder brother's son Song as son.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he adopted his elder brother's son Song as heir.

sentences.zh: 登謫甘肅，留家京師，嵩窘其衣食。

translations.literal: When Deng was relegated to Gansu, he left his family in the capital; Song constrained their food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng was exiled to Gansu his household remained in the capital, and Song stripped them of support.

sentences.zh: 登妾縫紉自給，幾殆，弗顧。

translations.literal: Deng's concubine sewed to support herself, nearly perishing, yet he did not attend to this.
translations.idiomatic: His concubine sewed for their bread; she nearly died of want, yet he took no action.

sentences.zh: 登還，欲黜之，以其婿於會昌侯，侯嘗活己，隱忍不發。

translations.literal: When Deng returned, he wished to dismiss Song, but because Song's son-in-law was with the Marquis of Huichang, and the Marquis had once saved his life, he concealed his resentment and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he meant to disinherit Song, but Song's ties to the Marquis of Huichang—who had once saved Deng's life—made him hold back.

sentences.zh: 及卒，嵩遂襲爵。

translations.literal: When Deng died, Song then inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng died, Song succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 後以非登嫡嗣，止嵩身。

translations.literal: Later, because he was not Deng's legitimate heir, the succession stopped with Song personally.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court ruled he was not Deng's legitimate heir, and the title ended with Song.

sentences.zh: 子參降錦衣衛指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Can was demoted to Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Can was reduced to a command in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 正統六年，與參將王真巡哨至伯顏山，遇寇擊走之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong, together with Vice General Wang Zhen he patrolled and reconnoitered to Bayan Mountain; they met raiders and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 6 he joined Vice General Wang Zhen on patrol to Bayan Mountain and repelled a raiding party.

sentences.zh: 次閔安山，遇兀良哈三百騎，又敗之。

translations.literal: Next at Min'an Mountain they met three hundred Urianghad horsemen and again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Min'an Mountain they met three hundred Urianghad horsemen and routed them as well.

sentences.zh: 追至莽來泉，寇越山澗遁去，乃還。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Manglai Spring, the raiders crossed mountains and streams and fled; they then returned.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued to Manglai Spring until the enemy fled across the mountains, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時謙已遷都指揮同知，乃以為都指揮使。

translations.literal: At that time Qian had already been transferred to Vice Regional Commander and so was appointed Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qian was already Vice Regional Commander and was now promoted to Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 八年充右參將，守備萬全左衛。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he served as Right Deputy General, garrisoning Wanquan Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he became Right Deputy General and garrisoned Wanquan Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 明年與楊洪破兀良哈兵於克列蘇，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: The next year with Yang Hong he defeated Urianghad troops at Keliesu and was advanced to Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he and Yang Hong routed the Urianghad at Keliesu and he was promoted to Vice Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 所部發其不法事，帝以方防秋，宥之。

translations.literal: His subordinates exposed his unlawful conduct; the Emperor, because autumn defense was at hand, pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates reported his misdeeds; with autumn campaigning near, the emperor let it pass.

sentences.zh: 復以北征功，進都督同知。

translations.literal: Again for merit on the northern expedition he was advanced to Vice Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Vice Regional Commander for his service on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 帝北狩，也先擁至宣府城下，令開門。

translations.literal: The Emperor went on the northern hunt; Esen led him to below Xuanfu's walls and ordered the gates opened.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was captured on campaign, Esen brought him to the walls of Xuanfu and demanded entry.

sentences.zh: 謙與參將紀廣、都御史羅亨信不應，遂去。

translations.literal: Qian with Vice General Ji Guang and Censor-in-Chief Luo Hengxin did not respond, and so they left.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qian, Vice General Ji Guang, and Censor-in-Chief Luo Hengxin refused, and Esen withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進右都督。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Right Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 與楊洪入衛，會寇已退，追襲之近畿。

translations.literal: With Yang Hong he entered to guard the capital; the raiders had already withdrawn, and they pursued and struck them near the capital districts.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to the capital with Yang Hong; the enemy had retreated, and they pursued them to the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 戰失利，洪劾之。

translations.literal: Battle met with disadvantage; Hong impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit failed; Yang Hong impeached him.

sentences.zh: 兵部並劾洪不救。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War also impeached Hong for not rescuing.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War impeached Hong in turn for failing to support him.

sentences.zh: 景帝俱弗問。

translations.literal: The Jing Emperor for both would not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing Emperor took no action against either man.

sentences.zh: 洪入總京營，廷議欲得如洪者代之，鹹舉謙。

translations.literal: When Hong entered to command the metropolitan army, court deliberation wished for one like Hong to replace him; all recommended Qian.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Hong took command of the capital army, court debated his successor; Zhu Qian was the unanimous choice.

sentences.zh: 乃進左都督，充總兵官，鎮守宣府。

translations.literal: He was then advanced to Left Regional Commander, served as commander-in-chief, and garrisoned at Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Regional Commander, made overall commander, and posted to Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年四月，寇三百騎入石烽口，復由故道去，降敕切責。

translations.literal: Jingtai year 1, fourth month: raiders, three hundred horsemen, entered Shifeng Pass, again by the old road departed; an edict was issued sharply reprimanding.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Jingtai, three hundred enemy horsemen entered Shifeng Pass and withdrew by the same route; the court sent down an edict sharply rebuking Zhu Qian.

sentences.zh: 逾月，復入犯。

translations.literal: Passing a month, again entered to violate.
translations.idiomatic: A month later they raided again.

sentences.zh: 謙率兵禦之，次關子口。

translations.literal: Qian led troops to defend against them, halted at Guanzi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Qian led his troops out to meet them and took position at Guanzi Pass.

sentences.zh: 寇數千騎突至，謙拒以鹿角，發火器擊之，寇少卻，如是數四。

translations.literal: Raiders, several thousand horsemen, suddenly arrived; Qian resisted with deer-horns, discharged fire weapons to strike them; the raiders slightly withdrew—thus several times, four.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand horsemen charged in; Qian blocked them with abatis and opened fire with firearms, driving them back briefly—four times in all.

sentences.zh: 謙軍且退，寇復來追。

translations.literal: Qian's army was about to withdraw; the raiders again came in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: As Qian's line began to give ground, the enemy pressed the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 都督江福援之，亦失利。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Jiang Fu rescued him; likewise met with loss of advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Jiang Fu came to his aid but was beaten back as well.

sentences.zh: 謙卒力戰，寇不得入。

translations.literal: Qian in the end exerted strength in battle; the raiders could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Qian fought on to the last and kept the enemy from breaking through.

sentences.zh: 六月復有二千騎南侵。

translations.literal: Sixth month: again there were two thousand horsemen invading south.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month another two thousand horsemen struck southward.

sentences.zh: 謙遣都指揮牛璽等往禦，戰南坡。

translations.literal: Qian dispatched Commander Niu Xi and others to go defend; they fought at Nanpo.
translations.idiomatic: Qian sent Commander Niu Xi and others to meet them; the battle was joined at Nanpo.

sentences.zh: 謙見塵起，率參將紀廣等馳援。

translations.literal: Qian saw dust rise, led Vice General Ji Guang and others in rapid rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing dust rise on the horizon, Qian galloped to the scene with Vice General Ji Guang and the rest.

sentences.zh: 自巳至午，寇敗遁。

translations.literal: From si to wu, the raiders were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: From mid-morning until noon the enemy was routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 論功，封撫寧伯。

translations.literal: Discussing merit, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Funing.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were tallied, he was created Baron of Funing.

sentences.zh: 是時，寇氣甚驕，屢擾宣府、大同，意二城且旦夕下。

translations.literal: At this time the raiders' spirit was very arrogant; repeatedly they harassed Xuanfu and Datong, intending that the two cities would before long fall.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy were then at their boldest, raiding Xuanfu and Datong again and again as though both cities might fall at any moment.

sentences.zh: 而謙守宣府，郭登守大同，數挫其眾。

translations.literal: Yet Qian guarded Xuanfu and Guo Deng guarded Datong; several times they broke the enemy masses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qian held Xuanfu and Guo Deng held Datong, and between them they repeatedly shattered the invaders.

sentences.zh: 也先知二人難犯，始一意歸上皇。

translations.literal: Esen knew the two men were hard to violate; only then with single intent returned the Former Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Esen saw that neither commander could be easily overcome and turned his mind wholly to sending the captive emperor home.

sentences.zh: 八月，上皇還。

translations.literal: Eighth month: the Former Emperor returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Former Emperor came back.

sentences.zh: 道宣府，謙率子永出見，厚犒其使者。

translations.literal: Passing by Xuanfu, Qian led his son Yong out to see him and richly rewarded his envoys.
translations.idiomatic: His route took him through Xuanfu; Qian brought out his son Yong to pay respects and lavished gifts on Esen's escort.

sentences.zh: 既而謙謬報寇五千騎毀墻入。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Qian falsely reported that raiders, five thousand horsemen, had destroyed the wall and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Qian sent in a false alarm that five thousand horsemen had breached the walls.

sentences.zh: 察之，則也先貢使也。

translations.literal: Investigating it, it was Esen's tribute embassy.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation showed them to be Esen's tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 詔切責之，謙惶恐謝。

translations.literal: An edict sharply reprimanded him; Qian in fear and trembling apologized.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sharply rebuked him, and Qian submitted in fear and shame.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: The next year, second month, he died at the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The following second month he died at his post.

sentences.zh: 贈侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as a marquis.

sentences.zh: 子永襲。

translations.literal: His son Yong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 謙在邊久，善戰。

translations.literal: Qian was long on the frontier and skilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had served long on the frontier and knew how to fight.

sentences.zh: 然勇而寡謀，故其名不若楊洪、石亨、郭登之著。

translations.literal: Yet he was brave but scant in stratagem; therefore his name was not like Yang Hong's, Shi Heng's, and Guo Deng's in being illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was bold rather than subtle, and his fame never equaled that of Yang Hong, Shi Heng, or Guo Deng.

sentences.zh: 成化中，謚武襄。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign he was posthumously titled Wu Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chenghua era he received the posthumous name Wu Xiang, Martial Succor.

sentences.zh: 永，字景昌。

translations.literal: Yong—style name Jingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, styled Jingchang.

sentences.zh: 偉軀貌，顧盼有威。

translations.literal: His frame and appearance were grand; in turning his gaze there was authority.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and imposing, with a commanding presence in every glance.

sentences.zh: 初見上皇於宣府，數目屬焉。

translations.literal: The first time he saw the Former Emperor at Xuanfu, several times the eyes were fixed on him.
translations.idiomatic: When he first met the captive emperor at Xuanfu, the emperor's eyes kept returning to him.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，嗣爵奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai reign he inherited the title and attended court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingtai he inherited the title and attended court.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，睹永識之曰：「是見朕宣府者耶？

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong restored the throne, seeing Yong he recognized him and said: "Is this the one who saw Us at Xuanfu?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, he recognized Yong and said, "Are you the one I saw at Xuanfu?"

sentences.zh: 」永頓首謝，即日召侍左右，分領宣威營禁軍。

translations.literal: Yong bowed his head in thanks; that very day he was summoned to attend at left and right, and assigned to command the Xuanwei Camp of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yong kowtowed in acknowledgment; that same day he was called to wait on the emperor and given command of a division of the Xuanwei palace guard.

sentences.zh: 天順四年，宣、大告警，命帥京軍巡邊。

translations.literal: Tianshun year 4: Xuanfu and Datong raised alarms; he was ordered to lead the capital army in patrolling the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 4, when Xuanfu and Datong sent alarm reports, he was ordered to lead capital troops on a frontier patrol.

sentences.zh: 七年統三千營，尋兼神機營。

translations.literal: Year 7 he commanded the Three Thousand Camp; soon he also held the Divine Engine Camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he took command of the Three Thousand Camp and soon added the Divine Engine Camp.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，改督團營，領三千營如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended, he was changed to supervise the regimental camps, leading the Three Thousand Camp as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong came to the throne, he was made supervisor of the regimental camps while retaining the Three Thousand Camp.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，荊、襄盜劉通作亂。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 1: the bandit Liu Tong of Jing and Xiang rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 1 the outlaw Liu Tong raised a revolt in Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 命永與尚書白圭往討。

translations.literal: Yong was ordered, with Minister Bai Gui, to go suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was ordered to campaign against him with Minister Bai Gui.

sentences.zh: 進師南漳，擊斬九百有奇。

translations.literal: Advancing the army to Nanzhang, they struck and beheaded nine hundred odd.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Nanzhang, they killed more than nine hundred of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 會疾留南漳，而圭率大軍破賊。

translations.literal: Meeting illness he remained at Nanzhang, while Gui led the great army and broke the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yong fell ill and stayed at Nanzhang while Gui led the main force to crush the rebels.

sentences.zh: 永往會，道遇余賊，俘斬數百人。

translations.literal: Yong went to join him; on the road he met remaining bandits and captured and beheaded several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Yong marched to join him, cut down stragglers along the way, and took several hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 其秋復進討石龍、馮喜，皆捷。

translations.literal: That autumn he again advanced to attack Shilong and Feng Xi; all were victories.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he campaigned again at Shilong and Feng Xi and won both engagements.

sentences.zh: 論功，進侯。

translations.literal: Discussing merit, he was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 毛裏孩犯邊，命佩將軍印，會彰武伯楊信禦之。

translations.literal: Molihai violated the border; he was ordered to wear the general's seal and join Baron of Zhangwu Yang Xin in defending against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Molihai raided the frontier, he was given the general's seal and joined Baron of Zhangwu Yang Xin in the defense.

sentences.zh: 會遣使朝貢，乃班師。

translations.literal: Meeting with envoys sent to offer court tribute, they then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Molihai sent envoys to offer tribute, and the army was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 六年，阿羅出寇延綏。

translations.literal: Year 6: Aluochu raided Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Aluochu invaded Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 復拜將軍，偕都御史王越，都督劉玉、劉聚往討，擊敗之蘇家寨。

translations.literal: Again appointed general, together with Censor-in-Chief Wang Yue and Regional Commanders Liu Yu and Liu Ju he went to suppress him and defeated him at Sujia Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made general and marched with Censor-in-Chief Wang Yue and Regional Commanders Liu Yu and Liu Ju, defeating Aluochu at Sujia Stockade.

sentences.zh: 寇萬騎自雙山堡分五道至，戰於開荒川。

translations.literal: Raiders, ten thousand horsemen, from Shuangshan Fortress divided into five routes and arrived; they fought at Kaihuang River.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand enemy horsemen came from Shuangshan Fort in five columns and gave battle at Kaihuang River.

sentences.zh: 寇少卻，乘勢馳之，皆棄輜重走。

translations.literal: The raiders slightly withdrew; riding the momentum they charged them; all abandoned baggage and fled.
translations.idiomatic: As the enemy wavered, the Ming cavalry pressed the attack and the raiders threw down their baggage and fled.

sentences.zh: 至牛家寨，遇都指揮吳瓚兵少，寇圍之。

translations.literal: Reaching Niujia Stockade, they met Commander Wu Zan with few troops; the raiders surrounded him.
translations.idiomatic: At Niujia Stockade they found Commander Wu Zan with too few men, and the enemy had him surrounded.

sentences.zh: 指揮李鎬、滕忠至，復力戰。

translations.literal: Commanders Li Hao and Teng Zhong arrived and again exerted strength in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders Li Hao and Teng Zhong came up and threw themselves back into the fight.

sentences.zh: 聚及都指揮範瑾、神英分據南山夾擊，寇乃大敗。

translations.literal: Ju with Commanders Fan Jin and Shen Ying separately held South Mountain and struck from both sides; the raiders then suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ju with Commanders Fan Jin and Shen Ying took the southern heights and struck from both flanks until the enemy collapsed.

sentences.zh: 斬首一百有六，獲馬牛數千，阿羅出中流矢遁。

translations.literal: Heads cut: one hundred and six; horses and cattle captured: several thousand; Aluochu, struck by a stray arrow midstream, fled.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred and six heads were taken and thousands of horses and cattle captured; Aluochu was wounded by a stray arrow and escaped.

sentences.zh: 時斬獲無多，然諸將鹹力戰追敵，邊人以為數十年所未有。

translations.literal: At the time the slain and captured were not many, yet the generals all exerted strength in battle pursuing the enemy; frontier people considered it what several decades had not seen.
translations.idiomatic: The body count was modest, but every commander had fought hard in pursuit, and on the frontier men called it the fiercest action in decades.

sentences.zh: 論功，予世侯。

translations.literal: Discussing merit, he was granted a hereditary marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was granted a hereditary marquisate.

sentences.zh: 阿羅出雖少挫，猶據河套。

translations.literal: Although Aluochu had met slight setback, he still held the River Bend.
translations.idiomatic: Though checked, Aluochu still held the Ordos.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，寇屢入，永所部屢有斬獲。

translations.literal: Next year, first month: raiders repeatedly entered; Yong's subordinates repeatedly had beheadings and captures.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month the enemy raided again and again, and Yong's troops repeatedly took heads and booty.

sentences.zh: 三月復以萬余騎分掠懷遠諸堡。

translations.literal: Third month: again with more than ten thousand horsemen they divided to plunder the stockades of Huaiyuan and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month more than ten thousand horsemen returned to pillage the forts around Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 永與越等分兵為五，設伏敗之，追至山口及滉忽都河，寇敗走。

translations.literal: Yong with Yue and others divided troops into five, set ambushes and defeated them, pursued to the mountain pass and Huanghudu River; the raiders were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Wang Yue split into five columns, ambushed the enemy, and drove them in flight to the pass and the Huanghudu River.

sentences.zh: 而遊擊孫鉞、蔡瑄別破他部於鹿窖山。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Mobile Corps Commander Sun Tang and Cai Xuan separately broke another division at Lucao Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Sun Tang and Cai Xuan, leading separate columns, routed another enemy band at Lucao Mountain.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，璽書獎勞。

translations.literal: Victory news arrived; an imperial letter by seal rewarded and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: When word of victory reached the capital, the emperor sent a sealed letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 永等再請班師，皆不許。

translations.literal: Yong and others again requested to withdraw the army; all were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and his colleagues twice asked to withdraw, and both times were refused.

sentences.zh: 寇復以二萬余騎入掠，擊退之。

translations.literal: Raiders again with more than twenty thousand horsemen entered to plunder; they were struck and driven back.
translations.idiomatic: When more than twenty thousand horsemen raided again, they were beaten back.

sentences.zh: 歲將盡，乃召永還，留越總制三邊。

translations.literal: The year was about to end; only then was Yong summoned back, and Yue was left as overall controller of the Three Frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: As the year drew to a close Yong was recalled, and Wang Yue was left in overall command of the three frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 十四年加永太子太保。

translations.literal: Year 14: Yong was added as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Yong was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，拜靖虜將軍，東伐，以中官汪直監督軍務。

translations.literal: Next year, winter: he was appointed Pacifying-the-Barbarians General and campaigned east; the palace eunuch Wang Zhi supervised military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter he was made Pacifying-the-Barbarians General for an eastern campaign, with the eunuch Wang Zhi supervising the army.

sentences.zh: 還，進爵保國公。

translations.literal: Returning, he was advanced in rank to Duke of Guaranteeing the State.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was raised to Duke of Guaranteeing the State.

sentences.zh: 又明年正月，延綏告警。

translations.literal: Again the next year, first month: Yan-sui raised alarms.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month Yan-sui sent alarm reports.

sentences.zh: 命永為將軍，越提督軍務，直仍監督，分道出塞。

translations.literal: Yong was ordered as general; Yue directed military affairs; Zhi still supervised; they went out of the passes by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was made general, Wang Yue directed operations, and Wang Zhi again supervised as they marched out by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 越與直選輕騎出孤店關，俘寇於威寧海子。

translations.literal: Yue with Zhi selected light cavalry and went out Gudian Pass; they captured raiders at Weining Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue and Wang Zhi took picked light cavalry through Gudian Pass and seized prisoners at Weining Lake.

sentences.zh: 而永率大軍由南路出榆林，不見寇，道回遠，費兵食巨萬，馬死者五千余匹。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Yong led the great army by the southern route out from Yulin; he did not see raiders; the road back was far, expending army grain in the tens of thousands, horses dead more than five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yong meanwhile led the main force south from Yulin, found no enemy, and made a long march home at vast cost in grain and more than five thousand horses lost.

sentences.zh: 於是越得封伯，直蔭錫逾等，而永無功，賞不行。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yue received enfeoffment as baron; Zhi's patronage rewards exceeded proper measure, while Yong had no achievement and rewards did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue was ennobled as a baron, Wang Zhi's clients were heaped with favors, but Yong won no credit and received no reward.

sentences.zh: 久之。

translations.literal: After a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward.

sentences.zh: 進太子太傅。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月，復偕直、越出師大同，禦亦思馬，獲首功百二十，遂賜襲世公。

translations.literal: Year 17, second month: again together with Zhi and Yue he went out as army to Datong, defended against Yisma, obtained head-merit one hundred twenty; thereupon he was granted hereditary succession as duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, second month, he again campaigned with Wang Zhi and Wang Yue from Datong against Yisma, took one hundred twenty heads, and was granted a hereditary ducal succession.

sentences.zh: 十九年秋，小王子入邊，宣、大告急。

translations.literal: Year 19, autumn: the Little Prince entered the border; Xuanfu and Datong reported urgency.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the nineteenth year the Little Prince crossed the border and Xuanfu and Datong sent urgent alarms.

sentences.zh: 越與直已得罪，以永為鎮朔大將軍，中官蔡新監其軍，督諸將周玉、李玙等擊敗之。

translations.literal: Yue and Zhi had already met with offense; Yong was made Great General Pacifying the North, palace eunuch Cai Xin supervised his army, and directing the generals Zhou Yu, Li Yu, and others he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Yue and Wang Zhi already disgraced, Yong was made Great General Pacifying the North; the eunuch Cai Xin supervised his army as he directed Zhou Yu, Li Yu, and the other commanders to victory.

sentences.zh: 還，仍督團營。

translations.literal: Returning, he still supervised the regimental camps.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he resumed command of the regimental camps.

sentences.zh: 或投匿名書言永圖不軌。

translations.literal: Someone cast an anonymous letter saying Yong plotted irregular conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Someone posted an anonymous letter accusing Yong of treasonous designs.

sentences.zh: 永乞解兵柄，不許。

translations.literal: Yong begged to be released from the military handle; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yong asked to lay down his command; the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 其冬，手敕加太傅、太子太師。

translations.literal: That winter, by the emperor's own brush he was added as Grand Preceptor and Grand Master of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor's own hand added him as Grand Preceptor and Grand Master of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年監修太廟成，進太師。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 4, supervising repair of the Imperial Ancestral Temple completed, he was advanced to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 4, when the ancestral temple restoration he oversaw was finished, he was promoted to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 永治軍嚴肅，所至多奏功。

translations.literal: Yong governed the army with stern solemnity; wherever he went he often reported achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Yong ran a tight army and reported victories wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 前後八佩將軍印，內總十二團營兼掌都督府，列侯勛名無與比。

translations.literal: Before and after, eight times he wore the general's seal; within he commanded the twelve regimental camps and concurrently held the Regional Military Commission; among the ranked nobles in meritorious name there was none to compare.
translations.idiomatic: Eight times he bore a general's seal, commanded all twelve capital regiments, and headed the Regional Military Commission—no other noble of his day matched his honors.

sentences.zh: 九年卒。

translations.literal: Year 9 he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died.

sentences.zh: 追封宣平王，謚武毅，子暉嗣。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xuanping; posthumously titled Wu Yi; his son Hui inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously created Prince of Xuanping with the temple name Wu Yi, Martial Resolve; his son Hui succeeded.

sentences.zh: 給事中王廷言永功不當公，朝議止予襲一世，後皆侯。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wang Ting said Yong's merit did not warrant a duke; court deliberation stopped at granting inheritance for one generation; afterward all were marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wang Ting argued that Yong's deeds did not justify a ducal line; court settled on one generation of succession, after which the heirs would be marquises only.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 暉，字東陽。

translations.literal: Hui—style name Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, styled Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 長身美髯，人稱其威重類父。

translations.literal: Tall in body, handsome in beard; people said his august weight resembled his father's.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and bearded, men said his bearing matched his father's.

sentences.zh: 又屢從父塞下，歷行陣，時以為才。

translations.literal: Moreover he repeatedly followed his father below the passes, passed through battle lines, and at the time was considered talented.
translations.idiomatic: He had often followed his father on the frontier and knew the ranks of war; many regarded him as capable.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年授勛衛。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 5: he was granted a guards post for meritorious nobles.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 5 he was given a post in the guards corps for nobles.

sentences.zh: 年垂五十，始嗣爵，分典神機營。

translations.literal: His years approached fifty; only then did he inherit the title, and was assigned to administer the Divine Engine Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Near fifty he finally inherited the title and was put in charge of the Divine Engine Camp.

sentences.zh: 十三年更置京營大帥，命暉督三千營兼領右府事。

translations.literal: Year 13: the great commander of the capital army was newly established; Hui was ordered to supervise the Three Thousand Camp and concurrently lead affairs of the Right Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the post of supreme commander of the capital army was reinstated; Hui was made supervisor of the Three Thousand Camp and acting head of the Right Commission.

sentences.zh: 火篩入大同，平江伯陳銳等不能禦，命暉佩大將軍印代之。

translations.literal: Huosai entered Datong; Baron of Pingjiang Chen Rui and others could not defend; Hui was ordered to wear the great general's seal and replace them.
translations.idiomatic: When Huosai struck Datong and Baron of Pingjiang Chen Rui could not hold him, Hui was given the great general's seal and sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 比至，寇已退，乃還。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, the raiders had already withdrawn; he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived the enemy had withdrawn, and he marched home.

sentences.zh: 明年春，火篩連小王子，大入延綏、寧夏。

translations.literal: Next year, spring: Huosai joined the Little Prince; greatly they entered Yan-sui and Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring Huosai allied with the Little Prince for a major invasion of Yan-sui and Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 右都御史史琳請濟師。

translations.literal: Right Censor-in-Chief Shi Lin requested relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: Right Censor-in-Chief Shi Lin asked for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 復命暉佩大將軍印，統都督李俊、李澄、楊玉、馬儀、劉寧五將往，而以中官苗逵監其軍。

translations.literal: Again Hui was ordered to wear the great general's seal, commanding Regional Commanders Li Jun, Li Cheng, Yang Yu, Ma Yi, and Liu Ning—five generals—to go, while the palace eunuch Miao Kui supervised his army.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was again given the great general's seal and sent with Regional Commanders Li Jun, Li Cheng, Yang Yu, Ma Yi, and Liu Ning, under the supervision of the eunuch Miao Kui.

sentences.zh: 至寧夏，寇已飽掠去，乃與琳、逵率五路師搗其巢於河套。

translations.literal: Reaching Ningxia, the raiders had already sated themselves with plunder and departed; then with Lin and Kui he led five-route armies to strike their nest in the River Bend.
translations.idiomatic: At Ningxia the enemy had already sacked the region and gone; he then joined Shi Lin and Miao Kui in a five-column strike at their camps in the Ordos.

sentences.zh: 寇已徙帳，僅斬首三級，獲馬駝牛羊千五百以歸。

translations.literal: The raiders had already moved their tents; only three heads were cut; horses, camels, cattle, and sheep—one thousand five hundred—were obtained and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had already struck camp; they took only three heads and drove home fifteen hundred horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 未幾，寇入固原，轉掠平涼、慶陽，關中大震。

translations.literal: Not long after, raiders entered Guyuan, turned to plunder Pingliang and Qingyang; Guanzhong was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the enemy took Guyuan and swept through Pingliang and Qingyang, throwing all of Shaanxi into alarm.

sentences.zh: 兩鎮將嬰城不敢戰，而暉等畏怯不急赴。

translations.literal: The two garrison commanders clung to their cities and did not dare give battle, while Hui and the others, fearful and timid, did not hurry to go.
translations.idiomatic: The two frontier commanders barricaded their walls and refused to fight, while Hui and his colleagues, timid and slow, lingered before marching to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 比至，斬首十二人，還所掠生口四千，遂以捷聞。

translations.literal: By the time they arrived, they cut twelve heads, returned four thousand captured people who had been seized, and thereupon reported a victory.
translations.idiomatic: When they finally arrived they claimed twelve heads, recovered four thousand captives, and reported a victory.

sentences.zh: 是役也，大帥非制勝才，師行紆回無紀律，邊民死者遍野。

translations.literal: In this campaign, the great commander was not talent for securing victory; the army's march was winding and without discipline; frontier people dead filled the fields.
translations.idiomatic: In that campaign the supreme commander lacked the skill to win; the army wandered in confusion without discipline, and the frontier dead lay thick across the countryside.

sentences.zh: 諸郡困轉輸餉軍，費八十余萬。

translations.literal: Many commanderies were distressed by transporting provisions to supply the army; the expense exceeded eight hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies across the region were bled dry forwarding supplies, at a cost of more than eight hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 他征發稱是，先後僅獲首功十五級。

translations.literal: Other levies and expeditions were the same; first and last they obtained only fifteen ranks of head-merit.
translations.idiomatic: Other summons and campaigns cost as much, yet in all they counted only fifteen head-merit grades.

sentences.zh: 廷臣連章劾三人罪，帝不問。

translations.literal: Court ministers sent memorials in succession impeaching the three men's crimes; the Emperor did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Officials submitted repeated indictments against the three commanders, but the emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 已而上搗巢有功將士萬余人，尚書馬文升、大學士劉健持之，帝先入逵等言，竟錄二百十人，署職一級，余皆被賚。

translations.literal: Already then over ten thousand meritorious officers and soldiers from the upward strike on the nests; Minister Ma Wensheng and Grand Secretary Liu Jian held them back; the Emperor had already taken first Kui and others' words; in the end he enrolled two hundred ten men, annotated one grade in office, the rest all received bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand men claimed merit for the Ordos raid, but Minister Ma Wensheng and Grand Secretary Liu Jian resisted rewarding them so lavishly. The emperor, having already been swayed by Miao Kui and his party, still enrolled two hundred and ten for promotion by one rank and bestowed gifts on all the rest.

sentences.zh: 及班師，帝猶遣中官賫羊酒迎勞。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Emperor still sent a palace eunuch bearing sheep and wine to welcome and console them.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the army's return the emperor sent a eunuch with sheep and wine to welcome the commanders home.

sentences.zh: 言官極論暉罪，終不聽，以暉總督團營，領三千營右府如故。

translations.literal: Censorial officials argued Hui's crimes to the utmost; in the end he did not listen; with Hui supervising the regimental camps, leading the Three Thousand Barracks right bureau as before.
translations.idiomatic: The censors denounced Hui at length, but the emperor would not hear it; Hui remained in command of the regimental camps and continued to head the right bureau of the Three Thousand Barracks.

sentences.zh: 子麒，襲侯，嘗充總兵官，鎮兩廣。

translations.literal: Son Qi: inherited the marquisate; once filled regional commander, garrisoned the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi inherited the marquisate, served as regional commander in the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 與姚鏌平田州，誅岑猛，加太子太保。

translations.literal: With Yao Mo pacified Tianzhou, executed Cen Meng, was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: With Yao Mo he pacified Tianzhou and executed Cen Meng, and was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，召還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 久之，守備南京，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time, garrisoned Nanjing in defense, died.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was posted to defend Nanjing, where he died.

sentences.zh: 子嶽嗣，亦守備南京。

translations.literal: Son Yue succeeded; also defended Nanjing in garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue succeeded him and likewise held the Nanjing garrison command.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中卒。

translations.literal: In the Longqing period died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Longqing reign.

sentences.zh: 四傳至孫國弼。

translations.literal: After four generations' transmission, reached grandson Guobi.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations later the line reached his great-grandson Guobi.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，楊漣劾魏忠賢，國弼亦乞速賜處分。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi period, Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian; Guobi also begged swift bestowal of disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Tianqi, when Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian, Guobi too petitioned for Wei to be punished at once.

sentences.zh: 忠賢怒，停其歲祿。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was angry; stopped his annual stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian in anger suspended his yearly stipend.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，總督京營。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen period, supervised the capital camps.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he commanded the metropolitan garrisons.

sentences.zh: 溫體仁柄國，國弼抗疏劾之。

translations.literal: Wen Tiren held state power; Guobi resisted with a memorial impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Tiren dominated the government, Guobi submitted a bold memorial to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 詔捕其門客及繕疏者下獄，停祿如初。

translations.literal: An edict ordered arresting his retainers and those who drafted the memorial, sent to prison; stopped stipend as at first.
translations.idiomatic: An edict seized his household clients and the memorial's drafters and imprisoned them, and his stipend was suspended again.

sentences.zh: 及至南京，進保國公。

translations.literal: When he reached Nanjing, advanced to Duke Protector of the State.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Nanjing he was advanced to Duke Protector of the State.

sentences.zh: 乃與馬士英、阮大鋮相結，以訖明亡。

translations.literal: Then he joined with Ma Shiying and Ruan Dacheng in alliance, until the Ming perished.
translations.idiomatic: He then threw in his lot with Ma Shiying and Ruan Dacheng and remained their ally until the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 孫鏜，字振遠，東勝州人。

translations.literal: Sun Tang, style Zhenyuan, a man of Dongsheng Subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tang, courtesy name Zhenyuan, was a native of Dongsheng Subprefecture.

sentences.zh: 襲濟陽衛指揮同知。

translations.literal: Inherited office as Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief of Jiyang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the post of assistant commissioner in Jiyang Guard.

sentences.zh: 用朱勇薦，進署指揮使。

translations.literal: Through Zhu Yong's recommendation, advanced to Acting Commander.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhu Yong's recommendation he was promoted to acting commander.

sentences.zh: 正統末，擢指揮僉事，充左參將，從總兵官徐恭討葉宗留。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengtong, promoted to Regiment Vice Commander, filled Left Assistant Regional Commander, followed Regional Commander Xu Gong to attack Ye Zongliu.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Zhengtong reign he was made regiment vice commander and left assistant regional commander, and joined Regional Commander Xu Gong against the rebel Ye Zongliu.

sentences.zh: 敗賊金華，復破之烏龍嶺。

translations.literal: Defeated bandits at Jinhua; again broke them at Wulong Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the rebels at Jinhua and again crushed them at Wulong Ridge.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，景帝召鏜還，超擢都督僉事，典三千營。

translations.literal: Yingzong on northern hunt, Jingdi summoned Tang back, leap-promoted to Censor-in-chief of Army, directed Three Thousand Barracks.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was taken north, Emperor Jing recalled Tang and leapfrogged him to vice commander-in-chief in charge of the Three Thousand Barracks.

sentences.zh: 也先將入犯，進右都督，充總兵官，統京軍一萬禦之紫荊關。

translations.literal: Esen was about to enter in invasion; advanced to Right Commander-in-chief, filled Regional Commander, commanded ten thousand capital troops to defend at Zijing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: As Esen was poised to invade, Tang was made right commander-in-chief and regional commander with ten thousand capital troops to hold Zijing Pass.

sentences.zh: 將發，寇已入，遂營都城外。

translations.literal: About to set out, raiders had already entered; thus he camped outside the capital wall.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could march the enemy was already at the walls, so he pitched camp outside Beijing.

sentences.zh: 寇薄德勝門，為于謙等所卻，轉至西直門。

translations.literal: Raiders pressed Desheng Gate; were repelled by Yu Qian and others; turned to Xizhi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders pressed Desheng Gate but were turned back by Yu Qian and others, then shifted to Xizhi Gate.

sentences.zh: 鏜與大戰，斬其前鋒數人。

translations.literal: Tang joined in great battle; cut their vanguard several men.
translations.idiomatic: Tang joined the great battle and cut down several of their vanguard.

sentences.zh: 寇稍北，鏜逐之，寇益兵圍鏜。

translations.literal: Raiders slightly northward; Tang pursued them; raiders increased troops and besieged Tang.
translations.idiomatic: As the enemy drew north Tang gave chase, and they rallied reinforcements and surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 鏜力戰不解。

translations.literal: Tang fought with all strength and could not be disengaged.
translations.idiomatic: Tang fought on without respite and could not break free.

sentences.zh: 高禮、毛福壽來援，禮中流矢。

translations.literal: Gao Li and Mao Shoufu came to rescue; Li took a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Li and Mao Shoufu came to the rescue; Li was struck by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 會石亨兵至，寇乃退。

translations.literal: Meeting Shi Heng's troops arrived; raiders then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Heng's troops arrived the raiders at last withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔鏜副楊洪追之，戰於涿州深溝，頗有斬獲。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Tang to assist Yang Hong in pursuing them; battled at Zhuozhou Shengou, quite had beheadings and captures.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to join Yang Hong in pursuit and fought at Shengou in Zhuozhou, taking a fair number of heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 師還，仍典營務。

translations.literal: Army returned; still directed camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he continued to direct barracks affairs.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，楊洪劾鏜下獄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai, Yang Hong impeached Tang and put him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingtai reign Yang Hong had Tang imprisoned on impeachment.

sentences.zh: 石亨請赦鏜，江淵亦言城下之役，惟鏜戰最力，乃釋之。

translations.literal: Shi Heng requested pardon for Tang; Jiang Yuan also said at the battle beneath the walls only Tang fought most fiercely; then he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng pleaded for his release, and Jiang Yuan testified that at the siege Tang alone had fought hardest; he was then freed.

sentences.zh: 三年冬充副總兵，協郭登鎮大同。

translations.literal: Winter of the third year, filled Deputy Regional Commander, assisted Guo Deng in garrisoning Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year he served as deputy regional commander assisting Guo Deng at Datong.

sentences.zh: 登節制嚴，鏜不得逞，欲與分軍，且令子百戶宏侮登。

translations.literal: Deng's control was strict; Tang could not have his way; wished to divide the army; moreover ordered his son, company officer Hong, to insult Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Deng's discipline was strict and Tang could not domineer; he sought a separate command and set his centurion son Hong to insult Deng.

sentences.zh: 帝械宏，竟以鏜故貰之。

translations.literal: The Emperor shackled Hong; in the end because of Tang's [influence] pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put Hong in irons, yet in the end pardoned him for Tang's sake.

sentences.zh: 召還，典三千營如故。

translations.literal: Summoned back; directed Three Thousand Barracks as before.
translations.idiomatic: Tang was recalled and resumed command of the Three Thousand Barracks.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，以「奪門」功封懷寧伯，尋予世券。

translations.literal: Yingzong restored rule; for "Seizing the Gate" merit enfeoffed Baron of Huaining; soon granted hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration he was ennobled as Baron of Huaining for the Seizing-the-Gate coup and soon received a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 天順初，甘肅告警，詔鏜充總兵官，帥京軍往討。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun, Gansu reported alarm; edict ordered Tang to fill Regional Commander, lead capital troops to go attack.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianshun Gansu reported an alarm, and Tang was ordered out as regional commander at the head of capital troops.

sentences.zh: 將陛辭，病宿朝房。

translations.literal: About to take leave at audience, illness lodged in the court chamber.
translations.idiomatic: While preparing his farewell audience he fell ill and lay overnight in the palace waiting rooms.

sentences.zh: 夜二鼓，太監曹吉祥、昭武伯曹欽反。

translations.literal: At the second watch of night, eunuch Cao Jixiang and War Vigor Baron Cao Qin rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch the eunuch Cao Jixiang and War Vigor Baron Cao Qin rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 其部下都指揮馬亮告變於恭順侯吳瑾，瑾趨語鏜。

translations.literal: His subordinate Regional Commander Ma Liang reported the revolt to the Conguan Marquis Wu Jin; Jin hurried to tell Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate Ma Liang reported the revolt to Conguan Marquis Wu Jin, who rushed to warn Tang.

sentences.zh: 鏜草奏，叩東長安門，自門隙投入內廷，始得集兵縛吉祥，守皇城諸門。

translations.literal: Tang drafted a memorial, knocked on the East Chang'an Gate, from the gate's crack threw it into the inner court; only then assembled troops to bind Jixiang and guard the imperial city's various gates.
translations.idiomatic: Tang drafted a memorial and slipped it through a crack in the East Chang'an Gate into the inner palace, mustered troops to seize Jixiang, and secured the gates of the Imperial City.

sentences.zh: 鏜走太平侯張瑾家，邀兵擊賊，瑾不敢出。

translations.literal: Tang ran to Peace Marquis Zhang Jin's house, invited troops to strike rebels; Jin did not dare go out.
translations.idiomatic: He ran to Peace Marquis Zhang Jin's house to raise troops against the rebels, but Jin dared not stir.

sentences.zh: 鏜倉猝復走宣武街，急遣二子輔、軏呼征西將士，紿之曰：「刑部囚反獄，獲者重賞。

translations.literal: Tang in haste again ran to Xuanwu Street, urgently sent his two sons Fu and Yue to call western-expedition officers and soldiers, deceived them saying: "Ministry of Justice prisoners broke jail; those who capture them receive heavy reward.
translations.idiomatic: In panic he fled to Xuanwu Street and sent his sons Fu and Yue to rally the western expeditionary troops with a lie: "Ministry of Justice prisoners have broken jail—heavy rewards for those who seize them."

sentences.zh: 」眾稍聚至二千人，始語之故。

translations.literal: " The masses gradually gathered to two thousand men; only then told them the real reason.
translations.idiomatic: When nearly two thousand had gathered he at last revealed the true cause.

sentences.zh: 時已黎明，遂擊欽。

translations.literal: The time was already dawn; then struck Qin.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn they were attacking Qin.

sentences.zh: 欽方攻東長安門，不得入，轉攻東安門。

translations.literal: Qin was just attacking East Chang'an Gate, could not enter; turned to attack East An Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Qin was battering the East Chang'an Gate without success and turned to East An Gate.

sentences.zh: 鏜兵追及，賊稍散。

translations.literal: Tang's troops caught up; bandits slightly dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Tang's men caught up and the rebels began to scatter.

sentences.zh: 軏斫欽中膊，軏亦被殺。

translations.literal: Yue hacked Qin in the upper arm; Yue also was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yue cut Qin across the upper arm and was himself slain.

sentences.zh: 欽知事不成，竄歸其家，猶督眾拒鏜力戰，至晡始定。

translations.literal: Qin knew affairs would not succeed; crept back to his home; still directed the masses to resist Tang fighting with strength; until afternoon only then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the cause was lost, Qin fled home yet still rallied his followers for a fierce fight until the afternoon before order was restored.

sentences.zh: 論功第一，進爵世侯，仍典三千營。

translations.literal: Assessing merit he was first; advanced in rank to hereditary marquis; still directed Three Thousand Barracks.
translations.idiomatic: Judged foremost in merit, he was raised to a hereditary marquisate and kept command of the Three Thousand Barracks.

sentences.zh: 贈軏百戶，世襲。

translations.literal: Bestowed on Yue [rank of] centurion, hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was posthumously granted the rank of centurion with hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 鏜粗猛善戰，然數犯法。

translations.literal: Tang was coarse and fierce, good at battle; yet repeatedly violated law.
translations.idiomatic: Tang was rough and warlike, yet repeatedly broke the law.

sentences.zh: 初賄太監金英，得遷都督。

translations.literal: At first bribed eunuch Jin Ying, obtained advancement to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he had bribed the eunuch Jin Ying and won promotion to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 事覺，論斬，景帝特宥之。

translations.literal: The affair was exposed; sentenced to decapitation; Jingdi especially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When this was discovered he was sentenced to decapitation, but Emperor Jing specially spared him.

sentences.zh: 天順末，以受將士賄，屢被劾。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianshun, for receiving officers' and soldiers' bribes, repeatedly was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: In late Tianshun he was repeatedly impeached for taking bribes from officers and men.

sentences.zh: 不自安，求退。

translations.literal: Not at ease himself, requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in his post, he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 詔解營務及府軍前衛事，猶掌左府。

translations.literal: Edict released camp affairs and prefectural army front guard duties; still held the left bureau.
translations.idiomatic: An edict relieved him of barracks command and of the Front Guard of the Metropolitan Army, but he retained the left bureau.

sentences.zh: 子輔請嗣，吏部言「奪門」功，例不得世傳。

translations.literal: Son Fu requested succession; Ministry of Personnel said "Seizing the Gate" merit, by precedent could not be passed to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu petitioned to inherit; the Ministry of Personnel ruled that Seizing-the-Gate honors were not hereditary by precedent.

sentences.zh: 帝以鏜捕反者，予之。

translations.literal: The Emperor because Tang captured the rebel, granted it to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted the succession because Tang had captured the rebel leader.
