sentences.zh: 傳子至孫應爵，正德中總督團營。

translations.literal: Transmitted son to grandson Yingjue; in the Zhengde period supervised the regimental camps.
translations.idiomatic: The line descended to his great-grandson Yingjue, who in the Zhengde reign commanded the regimental camps.

sentences.zh: 四傳至曾孫世忠。

translations.literal: Four generations transmitted to great-grandson Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: After four generations it reached his great-great-grandson Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中鎮守湖廣，總督漕運凡二十年。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period garrisoned Huguang; supervised grain transport altogether twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli he garrisoned Huguang and for twenty years oversaw the grain transport circuit.

sentences.zh: 又三傳至孫維藩。

translations.literal: Again three generations transmitted to grandson Weifan.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations later the line reached his descendant Weifan.

sentences.zh: 流賊陷京師，被殺。

translations.literal: Bandit armies took the capital; he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel armies seized Beijing he was killed.

sentences.zh: 鏜之冒「奪門」功封伯爵也，都督董興及曹義、施聚、趙勝等皆乘是時冒封，予世券。

translations.literal: Tang's falsely claiming "Seizing the Gate" merit to enfeoff as baron—Regional Commander Dong Xing and Cao Yi, Shi Ju, Zhao Sheng and others all took advantage of that time for false enfeoffments, granted hereditary patents.
translations.idiomatic: Tang had claimed Seizing-the-Gate credit for his barony; Regional Commander Dong Xing, Cao Yi, Shi Ju, Zhao Sheng, and others likewise won false enfeoffments then and received hereditary patents.

sentences.zh: 興、義、聚自有傳。

translations.literal: Xing, Yi, Ju each have their own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Xing, Yi, and Ju have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 趙勝，字克功，遷安人。

translations.literal: Zhao Sheng, style Kegong, a man of Qian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Sheng, courtesy name Kegong, was a native of Qian'an.

sentences.zh: 襲職為永平衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Inherited office as Commander of Yongping Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the post of commander in Yongping Guard.

sentences.zh: 正統末，禦寇西直門，進都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengtong, defended against raiders at Xizhi Gate; advanced to Assistant Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of Zhengtong he helped defend Xizhi Gate and was promoted to regional vice commander.

sentences.zh: 天順初，與孫鏜等預「奪門」功，超遷都督僉事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun, with Sun Tang and others anticipated "Seizing the Gate" merit; leap-promoted to Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianshun he shared in the Seizing-the-Gate honors with Sun Tang and others and was leapfrogged to vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 又與鏜擊反者曹欽，進同知。

translations.literal: Again with Tang struck the rebel Cao Qin; advanced to Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the rebel Cao Qin alongside Tang and was promoted to commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 孛來犯甘肅，勝與李杲充左右參將，從白圭西征至固原，擊寇，卻之。

translations.literal: Bolai invaded Gansu; Sheng with Li Gao filled left and right assistant regional commanders, followed Bai Gui west in expedition to Guyuan, struck raiders, repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: When Bolai invaded Gansu, Sheng and Li Gao served as left and right assistant regional commanders under Bai Gui's western campaign to Guyuan and drove the raiders back.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，典鼓勇營訓練。

translations.literal: Xianzong ascended; directed Valiant Drums Barracks training.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne he was placed in charge of training the Valiant Drums Barracks.

sentences.zh: 成化改元，山西告警，拜將軍。

translations.literal: Chenghua reign change, year one—Shanxi reported alarm; appointed General.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Chenghua reign Shanxi reported an alarm and he was made a general.

sentences.zh: 次雁門，寇已退，乃還。

translations.literal: Stationed at Yanmen; raiders had already withdrawn; then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped at Yanmen, but the enemy had already withdrawn, and he marched home.

sentences.zh: 明年復出延綏禦寇。

translations.literal: Next year again went out to Yan-sui to defend against raiders.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was again sent to Yan-sui against the raiders.

sentences.zh: 會方納款，遂旋師。

translations.literal: Meeting the opposing side offered submission; then rotated the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy sued for peace he withdrew his troops.

sentences.zh: 尋典耀武營。

translations.literal: Soon directed Glorious Martial Barracks.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given command of the Glorious Martial Barracks.

sentences.zh: 四年充總兵官，鎮遼東。

translations.literal: Fourth year filled Regional Commander, garrisoned Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became regional commander of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 七年召典五軍營，已，改三千營。

translations.literal: Seventh year summoned to direct Five Armies Barracks; soon after, changed to Three Thousand Barracks.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was recalled to command the Five Armies Barracks, then transferred to the Three Thousand Barracks.

sentences.zh: 乚加思蘭犯宣府，詔勝為將軍，統京兵萬人禦之，亦以寇遁召還。

translations.literal: Yesüzasan invaded Xuanfu; edict made Sheng General, commanded ten thousand capital troops to defend; also because raiders fled, summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: When Yesüzasan struck Xuanfu he was made a general at the head of ten thousand capital troops; the enemy withdrew before he arrived and he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 久之，進左都督，加太子太保。

translations.literal: After a long time, advanced to Left Commander-in-chief; added Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was made left commander-in-chief and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十九年封昌寧伯。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year enfeoffed Baron of Changning.
translations.idiomatic: In his nineteenth year of service he was ennobled as Baron of Changning.

sentences.zh: 勝初與李杲並有名。

translations.literal: Sheng at first with Li Gao shared fame.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was once as renowned as Li Gao.

sentences.zh: 後屢督大師，未見敵，無功，夤緣得封，名大損。

translations.literal: Later repeatedly supervised great armies, did not see the enemy, no achievement; by currying favor obtained enfeoffment—reputation greatly damaged.
translations.idiomatic: Later he repeatedly commanded large forces without meeting the enemy or winning merit, yet secured his title through court favor, and his reputation suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 後加太保，營萬貴妃塋，墮崖石間死。

translations.literal: Later added Grand Guardian, constructing Consort Wan's tomb mound; fell among cliff stones and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while serving as Grand Guardian building the consort Wan's tomb, he fell among the cliff rocks and died.

sentences.zh: 贈侯，謚壯敏。

translations.literal: Bestowed marquisate, posthumous style Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as a marquis with the style Zhuangmin, "Stalwart and Keen."

sentences.zh: 弘治初，孫鑒乞襲爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi, grandson Jian begged to inherit the nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign his grandson Jian petitioned to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 吏部言勝無功，不當傳世，乃授錦衣衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Ministry of Personnel said Sheng had no achievements; should not be transmitted to the world; then granted Commandant of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel ruled that Sheng had won no merit worthy of a hereditary title and appointed Jian commandant of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard instead.

sentences.zh: 範廣，遼東人。

translations.literal: Fan Guang was a native of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Guang was from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 正統中嗣世職，為寧元衛指揮僉事，進指揮使。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong reign he succeeded to the hereditary post, became Assistant Commander of Ningyuan Guard, and was advanced to Commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign he inherited the family post, became Assistant Commander of Ningyuan Guard, and was promoted to Commander.

sentences.zh: 十四年，積功遷遼東都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, through accumulated merit he was transferred to Vice Commander-in-Chief of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Vice Commander-in-Chief of Liaodong for accumulated merit.

sentences.zh: 廣精騎射，驍勇絕倫。

translations.literal: Guang was skilled at mounted archery and unmatched in fierce courage.
translations.idiomatic: Guang excelled at horsemanship and archery and was unmatched in boldness on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，廷議舉將材，尚書于謙薦廣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was taken north on campaign, court discussion nominated generals; Minister Yu Qian recommended Guang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was carried off on the northern campaign, the court debated whom to appoint as generals, and Minister Yu Qian recommended Guang.

sentences.zh: 擢都督僉事，充左副總兵，為石亨副。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Regional Commander, made Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief, and served as Shi Heng's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Regional Commander and appointed Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief under Shi Heng.

sentences.zh: 也先犯京師，廣躍馬陷陣，部下從之，勇氣百倍。

translations.literal: When Esen attacked the capital, Guang leaped his horse into the enemy formation; his subordinates followed, and their courage was increased a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen attacked the capital, Guang charged into the enemy line on horseback; his men followed, and their courage redoubled.

sentences.zh: 寇退，又追敗之紫荊關。

translations.literal: When the raiders withdrew, he again pursued and defeated them at Zijing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After the raiders withdrew he pursued and defeated them again at Zijing Pass.

sentences.zh: 錄功，命實授。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was ordered to receive substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His exploits were entered in the record and he was confirmed in substantive rank.

sentences.zh: 俄進都督同知，出守懷來。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Vice Regional Commander and went out to guard Huailai.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Regional Commander and sent to guard Huailai.

sentences.zh: 尋召還。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 亨所為不法，其部曲多貪縱，廣數以為言。

translations.literal: Heng's conduct was unlawful, and many of his followers were greedy and unrestrained; Guang repeatedly spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: Heng acted unlawfully, and many of his followers were greedy and unrestrained; Guang spoke against this repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 亨銜之，譖罷廣，止領毅勇一營。

translations.literal: Heng bore a grudge and slandered him until Guang was removed, retaining command only of the Yiyong Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Heng resented him, slandered him out of office, and left him with command of only the Yiyong Camp.

sentences.zh: 廣又與都督張軏不相能。

translations.literal: Guang was also at odds with Regional Commander Zhang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was also on bad terms with Regional Commander Zhang Yuan.

sentences.zh: 及英宗復辟，亨、軏恃「奪門」功，誣廣黨附于謙，謀立外藩，遂下獄論死。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, Heng and Yuan relied on their "Restoring the Gate" merit, falsely charged that Guang had joined Yu Qian's faction and plotted to enthrone a prince of the outer domains, and had him imprisoned and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne, Heng and Yuan, relying on their "Restoring the Gate" exploit, falsely accused Guang of siding with Yu Qian and plotting to enthrone a frontier prince. He was imprisoned and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 子升戍廣西，籍其家，以妻孥第宅賜降丁。

translations.literal: His son Sheng was banished to Guangxi; the household was registered for confiscation, and his wife, children, and residence were given to surrendered soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng was banished to Guangxi, his property was confiscated, and his wife, children, and house were given to surrendered soldiers.

sentences.zh: 明年春，軏早朝還，途中為拱揖狀。

translations.literal: The next spring, on his return from the dawn audience, Yuan on the road made gestures of bowing with clasped hands.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, on his way back from the dawn audience, Yuan was seen on the road making gestures of bowing with clasped hands.

sentences.zh: 左右怪問之，曰：「範廣過也。

translations.literal: Those beside him wondered and asked; he said: "Fan Guang is passing by."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants asked what was wrong; he said, "Fan Guang is passing by."

sentences.zh: 」遂得疾不能睡，痛楚月余而死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fell ill, could not sleep, and after more than a month of torment died.
translations.idiomatic: He then fell ill, could not sleep, and after more than a month of torment died.

sentences.zh: 成化初，廷臣訟廣冤。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, court ministers pleaded Guang's wrongful death.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign, court ministers pleaded that Guang had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 命子升乃襲世職。

translations.literal: His son Sheng was ordered to inherit the hereditary post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng was ordered to inherit the family post.

sentences.zh: 廣性剛果。

translations.literal: Guang's nature was firm and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was by nature firm and resolute.

sentences.zh: 每臨陣，身先士卒，未嘗敗衄。

translations.literal: Whenever he faced battle he led from before the soldiers and never suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he led from the front and never suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 一時諸將盡出其下，最為于謙所信任，以故為儕輩所忌。

translations.literal: For a time all the generals ranked below him; he was most trusted by Yu Qian, and for that reason was envied by his peers.
translations.idiomatic: For a time the other generals all ranked below him. Yu Qian trusted him above all others, and for that reason his peers envied him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：楊洪、石亨輩，遭時多事，奮爪牙之力，侯封世券，照耀一門，酬庸亦過厚矣。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Yang Hong, Shi Heng, and their like, encountering a time of many troubles, exerted the strength of claw and fang; marquisates and hereditary patents illuminated a single household, and the reward for service was also excessive.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Men like Yang Hong and Shi Heng lived in troubled times and threw all their fighting strength into service. Marquisates and hereditary patents lit up their households, and the rewards they received were excessive.

sentences.zh: 洪知盛滿可懼，而亨邪狠粗傲，怙寵而驕，其赤族宜哉。

translations.literal: Hong knew that fullness invites fear, but Heng was wicked, fierce, coarse, and arrogant, relying on favor and acting proudly; that his whole clan was exterminated was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Hong understood that great fortune invites ruin, but Heng was treacherous, brutal, coarse, and arrogant, trusting in favor and growing proud. That his entire clan was destroyed was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 朱謙勇略不及郭登，登乃無後，而謙子永，進爵上公，子孫世侯勿絕。

translations.literal: Zhu Qian's courage and strategy did not match Guo Deng's; Deng had no heir, yet Qian's son Yong was advanced to Grand Duke, and his descendants held marquisates in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qian's courage and strategy did not equal Guo Deng's. Deng left no heir, yet Qian's son Yong was raised to Grand Duke, and his descendants held marquisates without end.

sentences.zh: 孫鏜、範廣善戰略相等，而廣以冤死。

translations.literal: Sun Tang and Fan Guang were equal in skill at strategy, yet Guang died by wrongful execution.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tang and Fan Guang were equals in strategic ability, yet Guang died a wrongful death.

sentences.zh: 所遇有幸有不幸，相去豈不遠哉！

translations.literal: What they encountered had fortune and misfortune—how far apart were they not!
translations.idiomatic: What fortune or misfortune men meet in life—how wide the gap can be!
